title: FR-19 (MUST) broken: after 5 min of total provider outage the client hides every aircraft, so the map goes empty
evidence: interpolate.worker.js:5 `REMOVE_AFTER_S = 300`, and :53 `if (r.age_s > REMOVE_AFTER_S) return;` (age_s = now - seen_at). collector jobs/aircraft.py:44-50 and :69-90 return without publishing when no provider is available or a fetch fails, so seen_at never advances. WsHub.java:134-137 sends a full resync only from fanoutOne, which runs only on SnapshotUpdated, so no event means no snapshot with `stale=true`. ws.ts:99 diff handler hard-codes `stale: false`, which clears the STALE suffix whenever any diff (for example a global one) arrives. Design 10.1 says 300 s removal is server-driven ("서버가 remove 전송"), and FR-19 requires "외부 차단 상태에서 화면이 비지 않고 배지 표시". No E2E test covers FR-19.
failure_scenario: adsb.lol, adsb.fi and OpenSky are all unreachable (or the network drops) for 6 minutes. The api correctly keeps the last region snapshot, but in the browser every aircraft's age passes 300 s and the worker drops them all from the render set. At zoom 6 or more the map shows zero aircraft while the status bar still reads `aircraft 118`. This is exactly the empty screen FR-19 forbids. With a partial outage (region dead, global alive) the `· STALE` label also flips back off on each global diff.
fix: Take removal away from the client: keep aircraft rendered (opacity 0.4, not interpolated past 60 s) until the server sends `remove`. On the server, a scheduled 30 s resync should run even without SnapshotUpdated, so snapshots carry `stale=true`. Drop `stale: false` from the diff handler and derive stale from status.region.lag_s. Add a Playwright FR-19 test on the fixture stack that stops the collector and asserts aircraft stay visible plus the badge shows.
reason: Confirmed from code. interpolate.worker.js:5 sets `REMOVE_AFTER_S = 300` and :53 does `if (r.age_s > REMOVE_AFTER_S) return;`, where age is now minus seen_at (:16-17). jobs/aircraft.py:45-50 (no provider) and :71-93 (fetch error) return without publishing. StreamConsumer only publishes SnapshotUpdated on new stream entries, and SnapshotStore never expires states, so the api keeps the last region snapshot. That is correct server behaviour per design 5.1. A full resync (WsHub.fanoutOne, actually lines 152-155) resends the same old seen_at values, so it would not bring the aircraft back even if it ran. After 300 s with no provider, every region aircraft at zoom ≥ 6 is dropped from the render set. StatusBar still shows `aircraftCount` (aircraftStates.size, e.g. 119). This is exactly the empty map FR-19 forbids ("외부 차단 상태에서 화면이 비지 않고"). Design 10.1 (line ~1178) says removal is server-driven ("서버가 remove 전송"). Partial mitigation: the lag badge does turn red, because heartbeat sends status every 30 s and StatusBar reads status.region.lag_s. The `· STALE` suffix is lost, though: ws.ts:99 hard-codes `stale: false` on every diff (including global diffs). World-zoom (≤ 5) aircraft do not vanish, only because the world encoding drops seen_at (see GAP-2).
fix_v: 1) Client: in interpolate.worker.js and lib/interpolate.ts, stop dropping on age. Keep the aircraft (stale=true → icon-opacity 0.4, `estimated`), cap dead reckoning at 60 s rather than 300 s so stale icons do not drift, and delete only on a server `remove`/snapshot. Update tests/worker-sync and interpolate tests. 2) ws.ts:99: remove `stale: false` from the diff handler. Derive stale in StatusBar from `status.region.stale`/lag_s, which is refreshed every 30 s by heartbeat. 3) Optional: in WsHub.heartbeat, if the region snapshot's receivedAt is older than wsResyncIntervalS, call sendFull for subscribed sessions so snapshot.stale is recomputed. 4) Add a Playwright test on the isolated fixture stack: stop the collector, advance past 300 s (or lower the threshold via env), and assert aircraft features are still rendered and the lag badge is `bad`.

title: FR-11/FR-04/FR-05 (MUST) not met for global data: no 300 s world lag badge, provider mislabelled, and world encoding drops seen_at/squawk
evidence: StatusBar.tsx:13-14 `const regionLag = d.status?.region.lag_s ?? d.lag; const lagBad = regionLag == null || regionLag > 60;` never reads status.global. WsHub.java:168-169 SnapshotMsg carries `region.provider(), region.fetchedAt(), region.lagSeconds(now), region.stale(now, 60)` even though visible() now merges ~8,850 OpenSky states. AircraftController.java:58-65 iterates `snapshots.mergedValues()`, but meta is `Meta.of(req, s.provider(), s.fetchedAt(), 60)` (region), and lite features have no provider field. WsMessages.java:33-39: the world (zoom ≤ 5) encoding keeps only hex/lat/lon/alt_ft/track_deg/callsign, dropping seen_at, gs_kt, squawk and on_ground. The worker (interpolate.worker.js:16) then uses `seenMs = nowMs`, so every world aircraft reads as age 0 and never stale, and `emergency` (squawk 7500/7600/7700) is always false. FR-11 acceptance: "lag > 60 s(지역)/300 s(전세계)에서 배지 표시".
failure_scenario: OpenSky returns 429 or loses credentials, and the global snapshot is kept (currently lag 25.8 s, 8,851 aircraft per /api/v1/status). At zoom 5 the map shows thousands of aircraft frozen in place, fully opaque, labelled `source adsb_lol` with a green `lag 7s` badge, even after an hour without an OpenSky update. At zoom 5 a region aircraft squawking 7700 loses its red emergency highlight. REST /aircraft?bbox over China reports provider=adsb_lol for OpenSky positions.
fix: Add a global badge to StatusBar: show status.global.lag_s and turn it red when it exceeds 300 s. Send per-scope meta in snapshot messages (region and global provider/fetched_at/lag/stale). Keep seen_at (can be epoch seconds) and squawk in the world encoding so stale and emergency styling survive. In REST, add `provider` to lite properties or return per-scope meta. Add the FR-11 E2E test for both thresholds.
reason: Confirmed. StatusBar.tsx:13-14 uses only `d.status?.region.lag_s` and never reads status.global, although StatusService.publicStatus:49 already provides global.lag_s/stale (with a 300 s threshold). The FR-11 300 s world badge therefore does not exist. WsHub.java:186-187 (not 168-169) builds SnapshotMsg with `region.provider(), region.fetchedAt(), region.lagSeconds(now), region.stale(now, 60)` while `visible()` returns `snapshots.mergedValues()` (the live status shows 9,088 global aircraft). The status bar therefore reads `source adsb_fi` for OpenSky positions. AircraftController.java:65 sets meta from the region snapshot, and lite features (WsMessages.encode lite) have no provider field, so REST output mislabels the source. WsMessages.java:33-39: world encoding keeps only hex/lat/lon/alt_ft/track_deg/callsign. In the worker (:16) `seenMs = nowMs`, so dt=0 and stale is always false; emergency is always false because squawk is missing. When OpenSky pauses for credits (aircraft.py:105-106 pauses global until the next UTC day), about 9k frozen positions render fully opaque at zoom ≤ 5 with a green region lag badge. That violates the project's data-honesty rule.
fix_v: 1) StatusBar: add a separate global badge `world lag {status.global.lag_s}s`, red when status.global.stale (>300 s) and `—` when lag_s is null; show the global provider next to it. 2) SnapshotMsg: replace the single provider/fetched_at/lag_s/stale fields with `region:{provider,fetched_at,lag_s,stale}` and `global:{...}`, and update ws.ts/store accordingly. 3) WsMessages.encode(world=true): also emit `seen_at` (keep the ISO string so worker Date.parse keeps working), `squawk` and `on_ground`, so stale and emergency styling survive. 4) REST lite: add `provider` to properties (or per-scope meta) so OpenSky positions are not attributed to adsb.*. 5) Add an E2E/unit assertion for both thresholds.

title: WS resume after a hidden tab never refreshes alerts or SIGMETs, so the alert panel shows false INSIDE/PREDICTED entries (FR-10 MUST)
evidence: SkyWsHandler.java:78 `case "resume" -> { s.paused = false; s.needsResync = true; }` only triggers an aircraft snapshot (WsHub.fanoutOne → sendFull). WsHub.java:104/117 `if (s.subscribed())`: paused sessions skip `sigmets` and `alerts_batch`, and the full `alerts` list is sent only in sendInitial (WsHub.java:79-86, called from subscribe). Client ws.ts:62 `resume() { this.send({ type: "resume" }); setData({ conn: "open" }); }` sets "open" even when the socket is closed or in backoff. On reconnect (welcome, ws.ts:73-77) subscribe/select are re-sent but pause is not.
failure_scenario: The user switches tabs for 10 minutes. Meanwhile KAL081 LEFT a SEV TS SIGMET, a PREDICTION_CLEARED fires, another aircraft ENTERED, and AWC expires two SIGMETs. On return the panel still lists KAL081 as INSIDE and the cleared prediction with its old ETA, the new entry is missing, and expired polygons stay drawn. This persists indefinitely until the user happens to pan the map (which re-subscribes). If the socket dropped while hidden, the status bar shows `WS OPEN` during up to 30 s of backoff.
fix: On `resume`, call hub.sendInitial(s, engine.activeAlerts(null)) (snapshot + sigmets + radar + alerts + status) instead of only setting needsResync. On the client, set conn from the actual socket state, and re-send `pause` after welcome if document.hidden. Add a JUnit WS integration test for pause, event, resume and full alert state.
reason: Confirmed. SkyWsHandler.java:78 `case "resume" -> { s.paused = false; s.needsResync = true; }` only makes the next fanoutOne call sendFull, which sends aircraft only. While paused, `subscribed()` is false (WsSession:50), so WsHub.onSigmets (:122), onAlerts (:135) and the heartbeat status (:147) are skipped. The full `alerts` list is sent only in sendInitial (:97-105), which only subscribe() calls. The client's alerts map (ws.ts:108-123) is otherwise updated only by alerts_batch deltas. LEFT and PREDICTION_CLEARED events that happen while the tab is hidden are lost, so the panel and the SIGMET `inside` highlight (MapView:140) keep showing them until the user pans (moveend → subscribe). SIGMETs self-heal within about 300 s, because the collector republishes every poll, so that part is overstated. ws.ts:62 `resume()` unconditionally sets conn "open", even if the socket closed while hidden, until the backoff timer calls connect(). The welcome handler (ws.ts:73-77) re-subscribes, which sets paused=false on the server, and does not re-send pause when the document is hidden.
fix_v: Server: in SkyWsHandler case "resume", after `s.paused = false`, call `if (s.bbox != null) hub.sendInitial(s, engine.activeAlerts(null));`. That sends snapshot, sigmets, radar, full alerts and status, and replaces the bare needsResync. Client ws.ts: `resume()` should send resume and set conn only when `this.ws?.readyState === WebSocket.OPEN` (otherwise leave the connecting/closed state). In the welcome handler, after re-subscribing, `if (document.hidden) this.pause()`. Add a WS integration test: subscribe → pause → emit LEFT → resume → assert an `alerts` message that no longer contains the alert.

reason: Confirmed. build.gradle.kts:37-39 declares Testcontainers, but no test uses @SpringBootTest, MockMvc or PostgreSQLContainer. The api has 37 @Test methods across 6 unit test classes. title: FR-02 (MUST) OpenSky credit cap is 4,000/day (100%), not 2,880 (72%), and the region fallback spends 4 credits every 10 s
evidence: config.py:42 `budget_opensky: int = 4000`, :46 `opensky_reserve_credits: int = 400`. opensky.py:19-21 `supports_region = True ... region_cost = 4`. .env `AIRCRAFT_PROVIDERS=adsb_lol,adsb_fi,opensky`. jobs/aircraft.py:97-110: the reserve check only sets `_global_paused_until` (the global job); the region job keeps reserving until budget:opensky reaches 4000. FR-02 acceptance: "하루 크레딧 사용 ≤ 2,880(72%), 429 발생 시 다음 주기 자동 연장". NFR-06 allows OpenSky 72% as the only exception to ≤50%.
failure_scenario: adsb.lol is in 429 backoff (observed, VERIFICATION #10) and adsb.fi hits 3 failures (10-min cooldown). The region job falls back to OpenSky every 10 s at 4 credits = 1,440 credits/h. Together with global (120 credits/h), the account's whole daily 4,000 is gone in about 2.5 h. That is 100% of the free quota against the 72% acceptance, and the world view is dead for the rest of the UTC day.
fix: Set the OpenSky daily cap to 2,880. Give region fallback its own sub-budget (for example ≤ 10% of credits) or poll OpenSky for region no faster than 60 s. Apply the reserve check to both scopes. Add a budget unit test asserting total reservable credits ≤ 2,880 under a fallback scenario.
reason: Confirmed in code and live state. config.py:42 has `budget_opensky: int = 4000`, and live Redis `budget:opensky:20260927` shows limit=4000 (the About page describes 4,000 as the whole daily account quota). opensky.py:19-21 has `supports_region = True`, `region_cost = 4`. .env has `AIRCRAFT_PROVIDERS=adsb_lol,adsb_fi,opensky`, and ProviderChain.pick lets region fall back to OpenSky. The reserve check in aircraft.py:100-111 only sets `self._global_paused_until` on the job instance. That field is read only when need_global (:41), so in the region job it has no effect. Global alone is exactly 720×4 = 2,880 credits/day, so any region fallback pushes usage past FR-02's ≤ 2,880 (72%). Region can then keep reserving at 4 credits per 10 s (1,440/h) until the 4,000 cap, after which the global job also gets budget_exhausted for the rest of the UTC day. The trigger is realistic: adsb.lol 429 backoff is documented (VERIFICATION #10), and the live status shows region already on adsb_fi via fallback/recovery.
fix_v: Set `budget_opensky: int = 2880` (and BUDGET_OPENSKY in .env.example). Give OpenSky a region sub-budget, for example a separate Budget key `opensky_region` with ≤ 288 credits/day, or make region fallback to OpenSky poll no faster than 60 s. Apply the reserve check to both scopes: when remaining < opensky_reserve_credits, `chain.mark_down("opensky", seconds_until_utc_midnight)` in the region job as well. Add a pytest test asserting that the reservable total under a simulated all-adsb-down day stays ≤ 2,880.

title: CI E2E job always targets the wrong port: the stack starts on 8700 but Playwright defaults to 8701
evidence: ci.yml e2e job: `docker compose -f infra/compose.yml --env-file .env up -d --build --wait` (no SKYWX_PORT, so edge binds 127.0.0.1:8700 per compose.yml:15), then `npx playwright test` with no E2E_BASE_URL. playwright.config.ts:8 `baseURL: process.env.E2E_BASE_URL ?? "http://localhost:8701"`.
failure_scenario: On every push or PR the e2e job gets ECONNREFUSED on localhost:8701 and all 5 scenarios fail. Either CI is permanently red, or someone disables the job, and the FR-12 "fixture 모드에서 E2E 전부 통과" gate is never enforced.
fix: In CI, use the same isolated invocation as `make e2e` (SKYWX_FIXTURE_MODE=1 SKYWX_PORT=8701 SKYWX_NET_PREFIX=10.78.0 docker compose -p skywx-e2e ...), or export E2E_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8700 in the job.
reason: Confirmed. ci.yml:48 runs `docker compose -f infra/compose.yml --env-file .env up -d --build --wait` without SKYWX_PORT, so edge binds `127.0.0.1:${SKYWX_PORT:-8700}` (compose.yml:15). ci.yml:51 then runs `npx playwright test` with no E2E_BASE_URL, and playwright.config.ts:8 defaults to `http://localhost:8701`. Every E2E test gets a connection refused in CI. Makefile `e2e` sets `E2E_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8701` and uses the isolated `-p skywx-e2e` stack, and CI does not mirror that. The same area has another CI defect: the security job's Trivy `image-ref: skywx-api|skywx-collector|skywx-web` resolves to `:latest`, while compose tags the images `skywx-*:local`, so the scans cannot find them.
fix_v: In ci.yml e2e, set `env: { E2E_BASE_URL: http://localhost:8700 }` on the playwright step, or run the same isolated invocation as `make e2e` (`SKYWX_PORT=8701 SKYWX_NET_PREFIX=10.78.0 docker compose -p skywx-e2e ...`). In the security job, change the Trivy image-refs to `skywx-api:local`, `skywx-collector:local` and `skywx-web:local`.

title: NFR-14/NFR-10 CI gates missing: no JaCoCo or 80% coverage gate, no pip-audit, no mypy
evidence: build.gradle.kts plugins are only `java` and `org.springframework.boot` (no `jacoco`, no jacocoTestCoverageVerification). ci.yml collector step `uv run pytest -q --cov=skywx_collector --cov-report=term-missing` has no `--cov-fail-under=80`. The CI has `npm audit` but no pip-audit/uv audit, although NFR-10 says "npm/pip audit High 0건". mypy is a dev dependency (pyproject dev group) and design 14.2 lint lists `ruff·mypy·ESLint·spotless`, but CI runs only ruff.
failure_scenario: Backend line coverage can drop far below 80% (the api has no integration tests at all, see GAP-4) and CI stays green. A High CVE in httpx, pillow or numpy is never flagged. NFR-14 "백엔드 라인 커버리지 ≥ 80%" is unmeasured, so the README's quality claims cannot be substantiated.
fix: Add `jacoco` with `jacocoTestCoverageVerification { violationRules { rule { limit { minimum = 0.80 } } } }` wired into `check`, add `--cov-fail-under=80` to pytest, and add `uvx pip-audit` (or `uv pip audit`) and `uv run mypy skywx_collector` steps to the collector job.
reason: Confirmed. build.gradle.kts:1-4 applies only `java` and `org.springframework.boot`, with no jacoco and no coverage verification. ci.yml:14 runs pytest with `--cov` but no `--cov-fail-under`, and pyproject.toml has no [tool.coverage] fail_under. mypy is in the dev group (pyproject:27) and configured (:52-55) but never run in CI. There is no pip-audit step, although NFR-10 names npm and pip audit. NFR-14 (≥ 80% backend line coverage via JaCoCo) is therefore unmeasured. One partial refutation: Trivy image scans would cover Python site-packages, but they are currently broken by the `:latest` vs `:local` tag mismatch (see GAP-6), so Python CVEs really are not gated today.
fix_v: build.gradle.kts: add `jacoco` to plugins, `tasks.test { finalizedBy(tasks.jacocoTestReport) }`, and `tasks.jacocoTestCoverageVerification { violationRules { rule { limit { counter = "LINE"; minimum = "0.80".toBigDecimal() } } } }` wired with `tasks.check { dependsOn(tasks.jacocoTestCoverageVerification) }`. Run `./gradlew check` in CI. Collector job: `uv run pytest -q --cov=skywx_collector --cov-fail-under=80`, `uv run mypy skywx_collector`, and `uvx pip-audit` (on an exported requirements file from `uv export --no-hashes`). Fix the Trivy image tags.

title: NFR-08 restart safety (kill -9 → PEL reprocessing, ≤60 s recovery) has no test
evidence: StreamConsumer.java:144-150 drainPending() reads PEL with `ReadOffset.from("0")` and `count(50)` once per loop start, and bootstrapFromLastEntries() replays the last entry. No test exercises either path (no integration tests exist). Design NFR-08: "kill -9 후 Redis PEL 재처리 확인 테스트". PERF.md and VERIFICATION.md contain no restart measurement.
failure_scenario: If the api is killed with more than 50 pending messages across 4 streams (for example during a long GC pause while the collector keeps XADDing), only the first batch is reprocessed at startup. The at-least-once claim in README/ADR is unverified, and the 60 s recovery target has never been measured.
fix: Add a Testcontainers test: XADD N messages, consume without ACK (simulated crash), start a fresh consumer, and assert all N are processed and ACKed, including N > 50 (loop drainPending until empty). Add a scripted `docker kill -s KILL api` check to VERIFICATION.md measuring time-to-healthy.
reason: Refuted as a distinct defect. The failure scenario (more than 50 pending messages left unprocessed) cannot happen. StreamConsumer.consume reads with `count(10)` per stream (:156), and handle() ACKs in `finally` (:172-174), so at most 10 messages per stream can be pending (delivered but unACKed) at a crash. drainPending reads up to 50 per stream (:147), which covers that. Messages XADDed while the api is down are not pending. They sit after last-delivered-id and are read by consume() with lastConsumed ('>') after restart. The loop also re-runs drainPending on every consumer error. What remains is the missing kill -9 test and measurement, which GAP-4 already covers (the integration test suite).
fix_v: No separate fix. Include a PEL-reprocessing case in the GAP-4 Testcontainers suite: XREADGROUP without ACK, start a new consumer, assert processed and ACKed. Optionally record a `docker kill -s KILL skywx-api-1` time-to-healthy measurement in VERIFICATION.md.

title: Performance acceptance targets unmeasured or contradicted (NFR-01/03/04/05, FR-06/18/23/24)
evidence: PERF.md rows: NFR-01 "측정 방식 분리 필요" (Playwright 100-sample latency not done); NFR-04 "미측정" (3,000 aircraft ≥ 30 fps, JS ≤ 400 KB gzip, LCP ≤ 2.5 s), although ~8,850 global aircraft are now live; NFR-05 "JMH 미측정 … 미확정"; the api memory row claims "통과" from an earlier RSS 492 MB, while the k6 section of the same file reports "RSS 435 → 최대 722 MiB" and heap "따로 기록하지 않았다". A live `docker stats` shows skywx-api-1 at 633.1 MiB idle, above the NFR-03 budget of "메모리 ≤ 512 MB(api)". No measurement exists for FR-18 track p95 ≤ 100 ms (cache miss), FR-23 replay p95 ≤ 300 ms, FR-24 stats p95 ≤ 200 ms, FR-17 storage lag p95 ≤ 5 s, or FR-06 timeline switch ≤ 200 ms.
failure_scenario: A reviewer reading PERF.md sees NFR-03 marked as passing while the same document and the running container show 633 to 722 MiB. The largest-risk paths (global 8.8k-aircraft rendering, the replay query over a 220k rows/hour track_point, the track query) have no numbers behind the portfolio's performance claims.
fix: Measure and record: api heap via jvm_memory_used_bytes under k6 (and cap -Xmx to the budget or revise the budget in an ADR), Lighthouse ×5 for JS/LCP, a DevTools fps trace with global aircraft at zoom 3, a JMH benchmark for 10k×200, k6 scenarios for /aircraft/{hex}/track, /replay and /stats/*, and a Playwright timing loop for NFR-01 and FR-06. Correct the NFR-03 row.
reason: Confirmed. The PERF.md NFR-03 row states `≤ 512 MB 힙 | 컨테이너 RSS 492 MB … | 통과`, while the k6 section of the same file reports `RSS 435 → 최대 722 MiB` and says heap usage was not recorded ("힙 사용량 자체는 이번 측정에서 따로 기록하지 않았다"). A live `docker stats` shows skywx-api-1 at 640.8 MiB / 1 GiB. The design's NFR-03 measurement method is JFR plus docker stats against "메모리 ≤ 512 MB(api)". Heap max is about 616 MiB (G1 Old Gen max 645,922,816 B), so even the heap-only reading is not bounded by 512 MB. The 'pass' claim is therefore unsubstantiated. title: Unknown METAR ceiling shown as "없음", and the computed flight category turns missing data into VFR (data-honesty rule)
evidence: flight_category.py:16-18 `if ceiling_ft is None or ceiling_ft > 3000: return "VFR"` and :27-28 `if vis_sm is None or vis_sm > 5: return "VFR"`. :41-48 ceiling_from_clouds returns None both for CLR/NSC and for layers without a numeric base. weather.py:200-202 `cat = it.get("fltCat") or flight_category(ceiling, vis)`. In `flight_category`, return None when a needed input is unknown, rather than VFR, so the stored flight_cat stays NULL (the UI already shows '—'). title: Fabricated defaults: unknown values rendered as concrete 0 / "no" / "통과" (AircraftCard, stats, ops)

"yes" : "no"]` and :50 `["품질", s?.quality === 1 ? ... : "0 · 통과"]`: when `s` is null (the aircraft has left the snapshot; the REST detail returns `state: null`), the card asserts "no" and "0 · 통과". stats/page.tsx:23 `value: Number(traffic.find(...)?.value ?? 0)` zero-fills hours with no rows. title: Predicted-alert targets get no 10-min trajectory, and the selected-aircraft line ignores the server's 15° turn suppression

title: Alert list ETA is a stale snapshot (not counted down, updated only on changes of 30 s or more), and PREDICTION_UPDATED events spam the flash banner
evidence: AlertStateMachine.java:90 emits PREDICTION_UPDATED only when `Math.abs(prev.etaS() - p.etaS()) >= 30`. AlertPanel.tsx:56 renders `ETA {fmtEta(a.eta_s)}` statically. The lastEvent banner (:41-45) shows every PREDICTION_UPDATED event.

title: WS hello timeout is effectively 5–35 s (not 5 s), and pong timeout closes after 3 misses (not 2)
evidence: WsHub.java:120 `@Scheduled(fixedDelay = 30_000)` heartbeat is the only place checking `if (Duration.between(s.openedAt, Instant.now()).getSeconds() > 5) s.close(...)` (:125), and :128 `if (++s.missedPongs > 2)`. Design 9.5: "hello … 5 s 내 미수신 시 종료(1002)", "ping 30 s, 2회 무응답 시 종료".
failure_scenario: A client (or abuser within the per-IP limit) opens sockets without sending hello. Each holds one of the 200 global slots for up to 35 s instead of 5 s, a 7× amplification of slot exhaustion (1013 for legitimate users). Dead clients are held for 90 s rather than 60 s.
fix: Schedule a per-session 5 s hello deadline at afterConnectionEstablished (a virtual-thread or ScheduledExecutor task that closes with 1002 if !hello), and change the pong check to `>= 2`.
reason: Partly confirmed. The hello timeout is checked only in `@Scheduled(fixedDelay = 30_000) heartbeat` (WsHub.java:138-145, not :120-125), so an un-helloed socket survives 5 to 35 s instead of 5 s (design 9.5). The amplification argument is weak: a client that sends hello and answers pings can hold a slot indefinitely, and the per-IP cap is 5. The pong part is refuted. missedPongs is incremented before each ping, so `++s.missedPongs > 2` closes at the third tick, after two consecutive unanswered pings, which matches "2회 무응답 시 종료". The proposed `>= 2` would close after a single missed pong.
fix_v: In SkyWsHandler.afterConnectionEstablished, schedule a one-shot check (for example a shared `ScheduledExecutorService` or `Thread.ofVirtual().start(() -> { sleep(5000); if (!s.hello) s.close(CloseStatus.PROTOCOL_ERROR.withReason("hello timeout")); })`). Keep the pong check `> 2` unchanged.

title: ETag/304 missing on most public endpoints and Cache-Control lacks `public` (design 9.1 common rule)
evidence: Only AircraftController.java:55-66 (/aircraft) and WeatherController.java:59-73 (/sigmets) set ETag. Live: /api/v1/status → `Cache-Control: max-age=5` with no ETag, /alerts `max-age=5`, /radar/frames `max-age=60`, /airports `max-age=60` (no ETag, no public). title: Alert IDs are seeded from epoch seconds, so they collide after a restart: ENTERED inserts fail and LEFT updates close unrelated rows from the previous run
evidence: EngineService.java:41 `private final AtomicLong alertIds = new AtomicLong(System.currentTimeMillis() / 1000);`, and each ENTERED/PREDICTED takes ids.getAsLong() (AlertStateMachine.java:57,87). AlertRepository.java:51-54 `INSERT INTO alert_event (id, ...) VALUES (:id, ...) ON CONFLICT (hex, sigmet_id, kind, entered_at) DO NOTHING`, but the id conflict is on the PK (V1__init.sql:70 `id bigserial PRIMARY KEY`), which that ON CONFLICT does not cover. AlertRepository.java:60-61 `UPDATE alert_event SET left_at = :left WHERE id = :id AND left_at IS NULL`. Live evidence: the api log since the 11:19:24 restart has 131 lines of `duplicate key value violates unique constraint "alert_event_pkey"` (alert persist failed (ENTERED/PREDICTED)). In the DB, 121 rows that entered before the restart (entered_at < 11:19:20, ids 1790507963-1790508093) got a left_at after the restart. Only a new-run event whose id collided can do that, and those rows belong to different aircraft and SIGMETs.
failure_scenario: The previous run issued alert ids faster than 1 per wall-clock second (6,640 rows in about 3 h, bursts of 100+ per cycle), so its counter ran ahead of epoch seconds. After `make bench` or any api recreate, the new counter starts at the current epoch second, inside the range already used. New ENTERED/PREDICTED rows are rejected, so those alerts are missing from history. When those alerts later fire LEFT or PREDICTION_CLEARED, the UPDATE by id stamps left_at on an old, unrelated alert (another hex and SIGMET). Alert history, dwell statistics and the stats_daily aggregates are silently corrupted.
fix: Stop generating ids in memory. Either allocate ids from alert_event_id_seq (for example `SELECT nextval('alert_event_id_seq')` in blocks of 100 held by the engine), or seed the counter at startup with `SELECT GREATEST(COALESCE(max(id),0), extract(epoch from now())::bigint*1000)` and use millisecond-based seeds. Also make the LEFT, CLEARED and UPDATED statements also match on hex, sigmet_id and kind (`WHERE id=:id AND hex=:hex AND sigmet_id=:sig`), so an id mismatch can never touch another row.
reason: Confirmed in the code and the live DB. EngineService.java:41 seeds with `new AtomicLong(System.currentTimeMillis() / 1000)`. AlertRepository.java:51-54 `ON CONFLICT (hex, sigmet_id, kind, entered_at) DO NOTHING` does not cover the `id bigserial PRIMARY KEY` (V1__init.sql:70). The previous run's ids had run ahead of epoch seconds: at 11:15 the ids started at 1790507925 while epoch was about 1790507715, and at 11:18 the last id was 1790508093. The api restarted at 11:19:24 (log `Started SkyWxApplication`), so its seed was about 1790507962, inside the used range. Since then the api log has 131 `duplicate key value violates unique constraint "alert_event_pkey"` lines. The DB has 121 rows with entered_at before the restart (ids 1790507963-1790508093) whose left_at was set after the restart. Example: id 1790507963, hex 8a0378, entered 11:15:19, left_at 11:30:22. Only a colliding id from the new run can write those. PREDICTION_UPDATED (:58-59, `UPDATE ... SET eta_s, evidence WHERE id = :id`) also overwrites the evidence of unrelated old rows.
fix_v: Minimal fix: seed the counter in milliseconds, `new AtomicLong(System.currentTimeMillis())`. Alerts are issued far below 1,000/s, so a new run's seed is always above every id the previous run issued. Existing ids (about 1.79e9) are also below the new ones (about 1.79e12), so `ORDER BY id DESC` and cursor paging stay monotonic. As a guard, add the natural key to every id-based statement: `UPDATE alert_event SET left_at=:left WHERE id=:id AND hex=:hex AND sigmet_id=:sig AND kind=:kind AND left_at IS NULL`, and the same for PREDICTION_UPDATED. Then an id mismatch can never touch another row. Optional: log PK conflicts on INSERT at WARN with a counter metric.

title: WS fan-out blocks the single stream-consumer thread with an untimed Future.get(); one stalled client freezes ingestion for everyone for up to 20 s per send
evidence: WsHub.java:90-100: onSnapshot is a synchronous @EventListener on the stream-consumer thread. It runs `fs.add(pool.submit(() -> fanoutOne(s, ...)))` and then `for (var f : fs) { try { f.get(); } ...}` with no timeout. WsSession.java:64 `out.sendMessage(new TextMessage(json))`: ConcurrentWebSocketSessionDecorator lets the thread that holds flushLock run the delegate's blocking send, and Tomcat's default blocking send timeout is 20 s (verified in tomcat-embed-websocket 11.0.26: `DEFAULT_BLOCKING_SEND_TIMEOUT = 20000`). The decorator's 5 s limit throws SessionLimitExceededException, a RuntimeException (verified in spring-websocket 7.0.9). WsSession.java:66 catches only `IOException | IllegalStateException`, so the session is never closed and stays in the hub silently dropping messages. nginx.conf:67-68 `proxy_read_timeout 3600s; proxy_send_timeout 3600s;` keeps a non-reading client attached for an hour.
failure_scenario: A client subscribes to world view (full snapshot of about 8,800 aircraft every 30 s) and then stops reading: a mobile client in a tunnel, a suspended laptop, or a malicious raw socket. Once nginx and kernel buffers fill, the next fanoutOne for that session blocks in Tomcat for 20 s. WsHub.onSnapshot waits on that future, so the consumer cannot XREADGROUP. During that time no region snapshots, SIGMET updates, engine runs, alerts or diffs reach any of the other up to 199 clients. The stall repeats on every blocked send, and 5 connections per IP multiply it. NFR-01 (≤ 1.5 s) and the design 5.1 slow-consumer isolation are both violated.
fix: Do not join fan-out tasks on the consumer thread: fire and forget, keeping at most one in-flight fan-out per session and skipping the session with needsResync=true if the previous one is still running. If a join is kept, use one overall deadline (for example 200 ms) and abandon slow sessions. In sendOrDrop, catch SessionLimitExceededException (or RuntimeException) and close with 1008. Set the session user property `org.apache.tomcat.websocket.BLOCKING_SEND_TIMEOUT` to about 5000 ms in the handshake interceptor. Lower the /ws/ proxy_send_timeout to about 60 s.
reason: Mechanism confirmed. WsHub.java:108-118 onSnapshot is a synchronous @EventListener; there is no custom multicaster (grep finds no ApplicationEventMulticaster). It runs on the stream-consumer thread and does `f.get()` with no timeout (:116). ConcurrentWebSocketSessionDecorator runs the delegate's blocking send on the thread that holds flushLock. tomcat-embed-websocket-11.0.26 has `DEFAULT_BLOCKING_SEND_TIMEOUT = 20000` (checked with javap in the Gradle cache). No handshake interceptor sets BLOCKING_SEND_TIMEOUT. WsSession.java:67 catches only `IOException | IllegalStateException`, so the decorator's SessionLimitExceededException (a RuntimeException) escapes from non-lock-holder threads. Severity is lower than claimed. (1) The heartbeat closes a naturally stalled client after 3 missed pongs, about 60-90 s (WsHub.java:146), which usually happens before the kernel and nginx buffers fill. The realistic trigger is a peer that keeps sending `{"type":"pong"}` (SkyWsHandler.java:80 resets missedPongs) but never reads, or a client on a link slower than the world-view data rate. (2) The edge binds only 127.0.0.1:8700. (3) "never closed" is overstated: once the blocked send times out, Tomcat throws an IOException, which is caught and closes the session. The core defect stands: one such session blocks ingestion, the engine and fan-out for all clients for up to 20 s per stalled send. That breaks design 5.1 slow-consumer isolation (5 s limit, drop and resync).
fix_v: In WsHub.onSnapshot, do not join the fan-out futures on the consumer thread. Keep a per-session `AtomicBoolean inFlight`: if the previous fan-out is still running, set `s.needsResync = true` and skip; otherwise submit, and clear the flag in finally. Drop the `f.get()` loop and record fanoutTimer inside the tasks. In WsSession.sendOrDrop, also catch `SessionLimitExceededException` (or RuntimeException) and close with `CloseStatus.POLICY_VIOLATION`, so it is not left to the heartbeat. Set `attributes`/user property `org.apache.tomcat.websocket.BLOCKING_SEND_TIMEOUT=5000` in the handshake, for example `((StandardWebSocketSession) raw).getNativeSession().getUserProperties().put(...)` in afterConnectionEstablished, so the lock holder also respects the 5 s design limit.

title: Collector's live path depends on Postgres and Redis before every fetch, and infra errors fall into the scheduler's exponential backoff (up to 300 s); the local XADD queue is effectively unreachable
evidence: aircraft.py:44 `prov = await self.chain.pick(...)` leads to fallback.py:45 `if await self._status.is_disabled(name)` (Redis HGET). aircraft.py:55 `run_id = await ctx.db.start_run(...)` (INSERT) and :56 `await ctx.budget.reserve(...)` (Redis EVALSHA) all run before the HTTP fetch, with no try. weather.py:22 `_guard` does the same for sigmet, radar and metar. Status and heartbeat calls after publish (aircraft.py:132-154) are also unguarded. scheduler.py:34-38 `except Exception: failures += 1 ... delay = min(300.0, base * (2 ** min(failures, 5)))`. publisher.py:59-64 queues only when the XADD itself fails, which cannot be reached while Redis is down because pick() and reserve() already raised.
failure_scenario: Postgres restarts or is slow, or Redis blips. The region job raises in start_run or is_disabled, so nothing is fetched or published. Backoff grows 20 s, 40 s, 80 s, 160 s, then 300 s. A 5-minute DB outage leaves the realtime map stale for up to about 5 more minutes after the DB is back. If finish_run or status calls fail after a successful publish, the job is counted as failed and backs off anyway. This breaks design 5.1 ("실시간 경로는 DB에 의존하지 않음") and NFR-08 (60 s recovery), and the documented local queue (maximum 1,000) never protects a real Redis outage.
fix: Make ingest_run, quality and status bookkeeping best-effort: wrap it in try/except, buffer rows in memory and flush them later, and use run_id=None when the DB is unavailable. In pick(), treat a failed is_disabled as not disabled. Separate provider failures, which stay in the chain, from infra failures: retry those at the base interval, not with exponential backoff. Publish before any DB write. Only count run_once as failed when the fetch or publish failed.
reason: Confirmed. aircraft.py:44 `await self.chain.pick(...)` leads to fallback.py:45 `await self._status.is_disabled(name)`, which is a Redis HGET with no try. aircraft.py:55 `run_id = await ctx.db.start_run(...)` is an asyncpg INSERT (db.py:44-50) with no try, and :56 `ctx.budget.reserve` is Redis. All of these run before the fetch at :72. weather.py:22-23 `_guard` does the same for sigmet, radar and metar, and kma_radar.py:72-73 does the same. Post-publish bookkeeping (aircraft.py:132-154) is also unguarded, so a DB failure after a successful XADD still counts as a job failure. scheduler.py:34-38 then backs off `min(300, base*2**min(failures,5))`. For region (base 10 s) that is 20, 40, 80, 160, then 300 s. A DB outage of about 5 min can leave the next attempt about 300 s after the DB returns, so the realtime map stays frozen during the outage and up to 5 min after. That contradicts design 5.1 ("실시간 경로는 DB에 의존하지 않음") and NFR-08 (60 s). publisher.py:59-64 queues only when the XADD itself fails, so during a sustained Redis outage (pick() and reserve() raise first) the 1,000-entry queue is never used; it only covers blips between reserve and XADD. ctx.rt.refresh is guarded (runtime_settings.py:21-24), so the loop itself survives.
fix_v: Split infra bookkeeping from the fetch-and-publish path. (1) Wrap `start_run`, `finish_run` and `quality_events` in a helper that catches Exception, logs at WARN (rate-limited) and returns run_id=None; accept `run_id=None` in the envelope (`run_id="-"`). (2) In ProviderChain.pick, wrap `is_disabled` and `set_active`/`switch_event` in try/except and treat a failure as not disabled. (3) In run_once, if `budget.reserve` raises (Redis down), proceed with the fetch and let publish() queue locally. (4) Publish before any DB write, and wrap all post-publish status and DB calls in try/except, so that run_once raises only when the fetch or the XADD path fails. Then the scheduler backoff applies only to provider failures. Apply the same to weather.py `_guard`/`_ok` and kma_radar.py.

title: Open alerts are orphaned on every api restart: alert FSM state lives only in memory and nothing reconciles alert_event on startup
evidence: AlertStateMachine.java:37-38 `private final Map<Key, Track> observed = new HashMap<>(); private final Map<Key, Alert> predicted = new LinkedHashMap<>();` holds state in memory only. No startup code reads alert_event and none closes open rows (grep shows no ApplicationReadyEvent handler for alerts). DB: 2,129 alert_event rows with left_at IS NULL and entered_at before the 11:19:20 restart (1,739 OBSERVED and 390 PREDICTED). Duplicate episodes also exist, for example hex 71bf29 / RJJJ:I01 with 12 PREDICTED rows. Design 5.3 claims the FSM "(hex, sigmet_id) 상태를 보고 판단하므로 중복 이벤트가 생기지 않는다".
failure_scenario: Any restart (crash, `make bench`, image rebuild) loses FSM state. Rows that were open stay left_at=NULL forever, so /history shows them as never left and alert_dwell_avg_s excludes them. Aircraft still inside the polygon get a second ENTERED row with a new entered_at, so the same incursion is counted twice in alerts_by_kind.
fix: On startup, before the consumer starts, either (a) rehydrate the FSM from `SELECT ... FROM alert_event WHERE left_at IS NULL AND entered_at > now()-interval '12 hours'` as confirmed tracks that keep their DB ids, or (b) close them explicitly with an honest marker: `UPDATE alert_event SET evidence = evidence || '{"closed_reason":"api_restart"}', left_at = <restart time> WHERE left_at IS NULL`, and render the end time as unknown (—) in the UI rather than as a real exit time.
reason: Confirmed. The FSM maps are in-memory only (AlertStateMachine.java:37-38). The only ApplicationReadyEvent handler is StartupMirror (settings mirror), and nothing reads or closes alert_event at startup. The DB has 2,129 rows with left_at IS NULL and entered_at before the 11:19:20 restart (1,739 OBSERVED, 390 PREDICTED), and 453 (hex, sigmet_id, kind) groups have more than one open row. For example, 7504ac / WBFC:7:1790498400 OBSERVED has 8 rows, 6 of them open. The auditor's example 71bf29 / RJJJ:I01 (12 PREDICTED rows) is weak evidence, because only one of those rows is open and repeated PREDICTED and CLEARED cycles are normal; the multi-open groups are the real evidence. After the restart, every open row that is not in the current active set was checked against /api/v1/alerts, and none are orphaned by other causes, so the orphans come from restarts. MaintenanceJobs.java:95-98 dwell averages exclude them, and alerts_by_kind double-counts re-entries.

Load `SELECT id, hex, sigmet_id, kind, entered_at, eta_s, alt_ft_at_entry, evidence FROM alert_event WHERE left_at IS NULL AND entered_at > now() - interval '6 hours'` into `observed` as confirmed Tracks (inside=ENTER_CONFIRM) keeping their DB id, and PREDICTED rows into `predicted`. Normal LEFT or CLEARED then closes them with the real exit time. Close rows older than the cutoff honestly: `UPDATE alert_event SET evidence = evidence || '{"closed_reason":"api_restart","left_at_unknown":true}' WHERE left_at IS NULL AND entered_at <= cutoff`. Keep left_at NULL, render the exit as "—", and exclude those rows from dwell stats. Do not invent a left_at.

title: Hysteresis counts engine runs instead of new observations, so global (OpenSky) aircraft are confirmed ENTERED from a single position
evidence: EngineService.java:57-68: run() fires on every region snapshot (about 11 s), every global snapshot (120 s) and every SIGMET update. EngineService.java:80-81 `Map<String, AircraftState> all = new HashMap<>(snapshots.global().states()); all.putAll(snapshots.region().states());` re-feeds the same 120-s-old global positions every cycle. AlertStateMachine.java:52-54 `t.inside++; ... if (!t.confirmed && t.inside >= ENTER_CONFIRM)` has no check that seenAt advanced. DB check on the latest 400 OpenSky OBSERVED alerts: for 181 the previous track point was horizontally outside the SIGMET, and for 121 there was no earlier point within 10 minutes. So 302/400 (75%) were confirmed on one observation.
failure_scenario: A global aircraft's first position inside a polygon arrives with the global snapshot (inside=1). The next region snapshot about 10 s later re-runs the engine with the identical position (inside=2), so ENTERED is emitted, persisted and pushed. FR-09 ("진입 2회") and its boundary-flapping test intent are defeated for about 8,800 aircraft. A region aircraft is double-counted whenever a global or SIGMET event lands between two region snapshots.
fix: Store the last counted seenAt per Key and increment inside/outside only when `a.seenAt()` is newer (a new observation); for vanished aircraft, count outside once per snapshot of that aircraft's scope. Alternatively, drive hysteresis per scope: region tracks only on region events, global tracks only on global events.
reason: Confirmed. EngineService.run() is triggered by every SnapshotUpdated, whether region (about 10 s) or global (120 s) (:65-68), and by SigmetsUpdated (:57-63). :80-81 re-feeds the same global states on every run. AlertStateMachine.java:52-54 increments `t.inside` per run with no check that the observation is new (seenAt), and :69 increments `outside` the same way. A read-only DB probe covered the latest 300 OpenSky OBSERVED alerts, counting distinct track_point timestamps inside the SIGMET polygon (2-D) in the 6 minutes before entered_at. 220 of 300 had exactly 1 inside observation, so they were confirmed as ENTERED from a single position. That defeats FR-09 hysteresis ("진입 2회") for global aircraft. Exits are likewise confirmed after 3 engine runs of an unchanged position.
fix_v: In AlertStateMachine, add `Instant lastObs` to Track. In the hits loop, `AircraftState a = states.get(h.hex()); if (a != null && t.lastObs != null && !a.seenAt().isAfter(t.lastObs)) continue; t.lastObs = a.seenAt(); t.inside++`. In the exit loop, apply the same rule when the aircraft is present but outside (count only if seenAt advanced). When it is absent from `states`, count outside only on engine runs triggered by that aircraft's own scope: pass the triggering scope into step() and keep the scope per Track. Also keep evidence `confirmations` truthful.

title: Engine ignores observation age: predictions start from a stale position but ETA is measured from now, and frozen snapshots keep producing INSIDE/PREDICTED alerts
evidence: IntersectionEngine.java:61-63 `path[0] = new Coordinate(a.lon(), a.lat()); ... DeadReckoning.predict(a.lat(), a.lon(), a.trackDeg(), a.gsKt(), i * PREDICT_STEP_S)` and :77 `Instant entryTime = now.plusSeconds((long) tEntry);`. seenAt is never used. observe() at :35 filters only `!a.onGround() && a.altFt() != null`, with no staleness filter. The SnapshotStore is never cleared when all providers fail or `global_enabled=false`, yet EngineService.onSigmets (5 min) keeps running on it. AlertStateMachine.java:90 re-emits only when the ETA changes by 30 s or more, so a stale position yields a constant eta_s, shown as `ETA {fmtEta(a.eta_s)}` (AlertPanel.tsx:56).
failure_scenario: (1) Normal operation: a global aircraft's position is up to about 120 s old on every region cycle. At 480 kt it is already about 16 NM further along, so the ETA is overstated by up to about 2 min, beyond FR-21's ±60 s. The ETA also never counts down between global fetches. (2) FR-19, all providers down or OpenSky paused: frozen aircraft stay "INSIDE" and "ETA 4m" for hours. When data returns they all LEFT at once, which inflates dwell statistics. Estimates are computed from data that is no longer current, with no stale marking.
fix: Use data age: skip, or mark stale, aircraft with now − seenAt > 60 s (region) or > 300 s (global) in observe() and predict(). In predict(), advance the start point by (now − seenAt) before stepping, or report ETA as seenAt + tEntry − now. When the snapshot is stale, flag the alerts as stale (`evidence.data_age_s`) so the UI can grey them out instead of showing a live ETA.
reason: Confirmed. IntersectionEngine.predictOne (:59-83) starts the path at the reported position (`path[0] = new Coordinate(a.lon(), a.lat())`) and measures entry from `now` (:77 `now.plusSeconds((long) tEntry)`). observe() (:35) and predict() (:53-54) never read `a.seenAt()`. Global states are re-fed on every region-triggered run (EngineService.java:80-81), so their positions are up to about 120 s (plus provider latency) old. AlertStateMachine.java:90 re-emits only on a change of 30 s or more, and AlertPanel.tsx:56 shows a static `ETA {fmtEta(a.eta_s)}`. The ETA is therefore biased late by up to the data age and does not count down between global fetches. On part (2): FR-19 intentionally keeps the last snapshot with a stale flag, so retention is by design, but alerts computed from a stale snapshot carry no staleness marker (evidence has `seen_at` for OBSERVED only, and none for PREDICTED). The ±60 s criterion in FR-21 is defined on synthetic data, so the requirement breach is indicative, not proven.
fix_v: In predictOne, compute `long ageS = Math.max(0, Duration.between(a.seenAt(), now).toSeconds())`. Skip the prediction if ageS > 180. Otherwise report `etaS = tEntry - ageS` (skip if ≤ 0, since the aircraft is probably already inside, which observation will confirm) and evaluate `validAt(a.seenAt().plusSeconds(tEntry))`. Add `evidence.seen_at` and `evidence.data_age_s` to predicted alerts. In observe(), skip states with age > 300 s, or mark the resulting alert `evidence.stale=true`, and have AlertPanel grey out stale items. The UI can count ETA down from `judged_at` instead of showing a static eta_s.

title: Restart bootstrap restores only the newest skywx:aircraft entry, so the global snapshot comes back empty
evidence: StreamConsumer.java:133-137 `ops().reverseRange(s, Range.unbounded(), Limit.limit().count(1))` per stream, while region and global snapshots share the single stream skywx:aircraft (12 region entries per global). Current api log: `bootstrap done: region=109 global=0 sigmets=127 radar=13`.
failure_scenario: After any api restart, world view and global alert evaluation have 0 aircraft until the next global publish (up to 120 s), which breaks NFR-08's 60 s recovery. If global collection is paused (OpenSky credit reserve until UTC midnight, budget exhausted, or global_enabled=false), the global snapshot stays empty for hours although valid global entries are still in the stream. Status then shows global aircraft 0 and NO DATA.
fix: Scan backwards (for example XREVRANGE COUNT 50, or page until both found) and bootstrap the newest entry for each scope (region and global). Alternatively, publish global snapshots to their own stream (skywx:aircraft:global) with a small MAXLEN.
reason: Confirmed. StreamConsumer.java:133-137 takes `reverseRange(s, Range.unbounded(), Limit.limit().count(1))`, which is only the newest entry, while region and global share skywx:aircraft. The live api log shows `bootstrap done: region=109 global=0 sigmets=127 radar=13`. consume() then reads only undelivered entries, and the last global entry was already ACKed by the previous run, so world view and global alert evaluation have 0 global aircraft until the next global publish (≤ 120 s). The "stays empty for hours" part is overstated. The stream is MAXLEN ~200 (publisher.py:21), about 30 min of entries, so a paused global's last entry is trimmed within about half an hour, and restoring hours-old global data would itself be stale. The real impact is a gap of up to 2 min after each api restart, beyond NFR-08's 60 s.
fix_v: In bootstrapFromLastEntries for S_AIRCRAFT, read `reverseRange(S_AIRCRAFT, Range.unbounded(), Limit.limit().count(30))`, iterate newest to oldest, and process the first entry per `scope` (region and global), processing the global one first so the region overlay wins. Skip an entry whose fetched_at is older than 10 min, so stale data is not restored as live.

title: Stream backlog replay rolls the live snapshot back to stale data after downtime; no monotonic fetched_at guard
evidence: StreamConsumer.java:105-108 runs `bootstrapFromLastEntries(); drainPending(); consume();`: bootstrap applies the newest entry, then consume() uses `ReadOffset.lastConsumed()` (:155), which is XREADGROUP > and returns every unread entry oldest-first. :205-206 `Snapshot prev = snapshots.replace(snap);` and SnapshotStore.java:22-24 `global.getAndSet(s) : region.getAndSet(s)` replace unconditionally. The loop also re-runs bootstrap after every transient error (:109-113). publisher.py:52-58 flushes up to 1,000 queued old snapshots in order. Design 5.2: "스냅샷은 '최신만 의미'".
failure_scenario: The api is down for 10 minutes (crash loop, DB unavailable at Flyway). On start the map briefly shows current data, then jumps back 10 minutes and replays about 55 region and 5 global snapshots; each global takes about 2.7 s (see REL-9), so this lasts about 15-20 s. Meanwhile the engine judges 10-minute-old positions with Instant.now(), so it persists ENTERED/LEFT/PREDICTED rows with wrong times and emits WS alert events for positions that are no longer true.
fix: In aircraft(), if fetchedAt is not after the current snapshot's fetchedAt for that scope, skip the live replace and the engine and WS events. Still hand the states to TrackWriter so history stays complete (at-least-once). Apply the same guard to sigmet and radar via fetchedAt or generated. Only re-bootstrap when the group was recreated.
reason: Confirmed. loop() (:102-114) runs bootstrap (newest entry applied) → drainPending → consume() with `ReadOffset.lastConsumed()` (:155), which returns all undelivered entries oldest-first. aircraft() (:198-208) calls `snapshots.replace(snap)` unconditionally (SnapshotStore.java:44-46) and publishes SnapshotUpdated for each. The `live` flag passed to process() is never used by aircraft(), sigmet() or radar(). After any downtime longer than one poll interval, the map and the engine step back to the oldest backlog entry and replay forward. The engine judges those positions with `Instant.now()` (EngineService.java:67), so persisted ENTERED/LEFT/PREDICTED times are wrong. Global replay is slow (skywx_stream_process_seconds p95 is about 2.55 s, max 2.88 s, now). Any transient consumer error re-runs bootstrap (:106), then resumes older unread entries, which causes the same rollback.
fix_v: In StreamConsumer.aircraft(), compare against the current snapshot of the same scope: `Snapshot cur = "global".equals(scope) ? snapshots.global() : snapshots.region(); if (!fetchedAt.isAfter(cur.fetchedAt())) { events.publishEvent(new IngestEvents.BacklogStates(states.values())); return; }`, and have TrackWriter also listen to BacklogStates, so track history stays complete and at-least-once without a live replace, engine run or WS fan-out. Apply the same `fetchedAt` monotonic guard in sigmet() (against sigmets.state().fetchedAt()) and radar() (against radar.frames().fetchedAt()). Run bootstrapFromLastEntries only once per process start, not on every retry.

title: aircraft static-info upsert runs synchronously on the stream-consumer thread, one INSERT per aircraft (about 8,800 per global snapshot)
evidence: TrackWriter.java:52-61: the @EventListener onSnapshot, on the consumer thread, calls `aircraft.touch(e.current().states().values());`. AircraftRepository.java:23-37 filters hex not touched in 60 s, then does one `db.sql("INSERT INTO aircraft ... ON CONFLICT ...").update()` per aircraft. Global snapshots come every 120 s, so all about 8,800 are due each time. Prometheus: skywx_stream_process_seconds p95=2.684 s and max=2.667 s, versus skywx_engine_cycle_seconds p95=0.037 s and skywx_ws_fanout_seconds p95=0.0047 s. The difference is the touch loop. When the DB is down, each call waits Hikari connection-timeout 5000 ms (application.yml) before the catch.
failure_scenario: Each global snapshot holds the consumer for about 2.7 s, and a region snapshot arriving then waits behind it, which pushes NFR-01 (p95 ≤ 1.5 s end-to-end) past its limit on those cycles. During a DB outage or nightly jobs, every snapshot costs about 5 s before the exception is swallowed, so the live map lags because of the DB. That contradicts "실시간 경로는 DB에 의존하지 않음".
fix: Move touch() off the consumer: hand states to the TrackWriter virtual-thread worker (or a separate queue). Batch the upsert (`INSERT ... SELECT * FROM unnest(:hex[], :reg[], ...) ON CONFLICT ...` or jdbc.batchUpdate). Only write hex values that are new, or whose registration or type changed; derive last_seen from track_point or update it hourly.
reason: Confirmed. TrackWriter.onSnapshot (:52-62) runs on the consumer thread and calls `aircraft.touch(...)`. AircraftRepository.touch (:21-42) runs one `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT` round trip per due aircraft. Due means 60 s since last touch, so every aircraft in a 120-s global snapshot is due. Live evidence: skywx_stream_process_seconds p95=2.55 s and max=2.88 s, against engine cycle p95=0.035 s and ws fan-out p95=0.0017 s; the aircraft table shows n_tup_upd=569,342 in about 3.5 h (about 45 per second). JSON schema validation of the global payload also contributes, but touch is the dominant cost. On DB outage, the first insert waits Hikari `connection-timeout: 5000` (application.yml:14) before the catch, and lastTouched is not updated, so every subsequent snapshot also pays about 5 s on the consumer thread.
fix_v: Remove `aircraft.touch(...)` from TrackWriter.onSnapshot and run it on the track-writer virtual thread. For example, enqueue the snapshot's states into a small `BlockingQueue<Collection<AircraftState>>` drained by the worker. Replace the per-row loop with one batched statement: `jdbc.batchUpdate(sql, due, 1000, setter)` or `INSERT ... SELECT * FROM unnest(?::char(6)[], ?::text[], ...) ON CONFLICT ...`. Only upsert hexes that are new or whose registration, type or category changed. Update last_seen at most every 10-15 min per hex.

title: TrackWriter silently discards a failed batch: a DB outage loses all track rows while the dropped metric stays 0
evidence: TrackWriter.java:71-83 `AircraftState first = queue.poll(...); ... queue.drainTo(batch, BATCH - 1); write(batch); } catch (Exception e) { log.warn("track batch failed: {}", e.toString()); sleep(2000); }`. The batch is lost and droppedRows is incremented only on queue overflow (:55-58). Design 5.1: "비동기 배치 큐(메모리 상한 50,000행, 초과 시 오래된 것부터 드롭 + 지표)".
failure_scenario: Postgres is down for 5 minutes. The worker takes up to 2,000 rows, write() fails after the 5 s connection timeout, and those rows are gone, then it sleeps 2 s. It discards about 285 rows/s, faster than ingest (about 85 rows/s), so the 50,000-row buffer never holds anything. After recovery the 5-minute gap is permanent, yet skywx_track_rows_total{result="dropped"} still reads 0, so operators get no signal. The same applies to a missing partition.
fix: On failure, keep the batch (re-offer it at the head, or hold a pending list) and retry with backoff, dropping oldest only when QUEUE_MAX is exceeded. Count every discarded row, including permanent SQL errors after N retries, in skywx_track_rows_total{result="dropped"} or a new result="failed" tag.
reason: Confirmed. TrackWriter.loop (:68-85) drains up to 2,000 rows, and on any exception from write() logs `track batch failed` and sleeps 2 s. The batch is discarded, and droppedRows is incremented only on queue overflow (:55-58). During a DB outage each cycle waits about 5 s (Hikari connection timeout) and then about 2 s asleep. Ingest is about 85 rows/s (about 11/s region plus about 73/s global), so each batch takes every queued row and discards it; the 50,000-row buffer from design 5.1 never retains anything. Live: skywx_track_rows_total{result="dropped"} = 0. The same silent loss happens for a missing partition.
fix_v: On failure, keep the batch. Hold `List<AircraftState> pending` in the worker and retry it with backoff (2 s, 4 s, up to 30 s) before draining more. While pending, new rows keep accumulating in the queue, and overflow drops oldest with droppedRows++ as designed. For non-transient SQL errors (SQLState class 22/23/42, or 3 retries on the same batch), drop the batch and count it via `Counter.builder("skywx_track_rows_total").tag("result","failed")`.

title: Nightly retention fails on permissions: skywx_api cannot DELETE metar_obs, radar_frame or ingest_run, so those tables grow without bound
evidence: MaintenanceJobs.java:46-48 `db.sql("DELETE FROM metar_obs WHERE ...").update(); db.sql("DELETE FROM radar_frame ...").update(); db.sql("DELETE FROM ingest_run ...").update();` all inside one try block (:41-51). Distinct from the known partition-function issue.

No role ever purges ingest_run, quality_event (cascade from ingest_run), metar_obs or radar_frame. NFR-09 retention is not met and the database grows indefinitely.

The quality_event cascade from ingest_run would run as the table owner anyway, but an explicit grant is harmless. In MaintenanceJobs.dropOldPartitions, wrap each statement in its own try/catch with its own log line, so one failure does not skip the rest. title: A partial SIGMET fetch (US AIR/SIGMET failure) publishes an incomplete set that the api treats as authoritative, causing false LEFT events and duplicate alerts
evidence: weather.py:125-129 `try: us = await self.awc.airsigmet() except Exception: ... us = None`, and then :92-97 US SIGMETs are appended only when `us is not None`, and the set is published as a full snapshot (:104-114). SigmetStore.java:22-25 `state.set(new State(..., byId))` is a full replace. EngineService.java:57-62 rebuilds the index from `e.state().byId()`, and AlertStateMachine.java:72-75 emits LEFT after 3 cycles out of the index.
failure_scenario: airsigmet.json times out once while isigmet succeeds. All US SIGMETs/G-AIRMETs disappear from the map and the engine index for 5 minutes. Aircraft inside them get LEFT events (left_at = now, persisted and pushed) after about 30 s, and are re-ENTERED with new rows at the next successful fetch. The map shows no hazard where one is still valid, which violates the data-honesty rule, and the alert history gains fake exit and re-entry pairs.
fix: When the US fetch fails, carry forward the previous US records (keeping their original fetched_at and provider), or publish per source (for example scope="isigmet"/"airsigmet") and have SigmetStore replace only the records of the providers present in the message, marking that source stale in status.
reason: Confirmed. weather.py:123-130 swallows an airsigmet failure (`us = None`). :89-97 then builds the set from international SIGMETs only and publishes it as a full snapshot (:104-114). SigmetStore.replace (:22-26) replaces the whole map, EngineService.onSigmets (:57-63) rebuilds the index from it, and AlertStateMachine (:64-76) emits LEFT after 3 engine runs without hits, then new ENTERED rows when US SIGMETs return. No airsigmet failure occurred in the current collector log (0 matches), but the path is explicitly coded as tolerated, and AWC timeouts are a normal failure mode (the collector uses an 8 s timeout, config.py:55). When airsigmet fails, append the members of `_last_us` whose `valid_to > now`, unchanged (original provider and fetched_at), and record `ctx.status.failure('awc', ...)` with scope airsigmet, so /status shows that part as stale. Clear `_last_us` only after a successful fetch.

title: Expired SIGMETs stay on clients' maps as "active" when no new SIGMET message arrives (for example during an AWC outage)
evidence: WsHub.java:104-107 sends the SIGMET collection only on SigmetsUpdated (collector every 300 s) and at subscribe. SigmetGeoJson.java:20,42 filter and set `props.put("active", s.validAt(now))` at send time only. EngineService.java:71-75 `rebuildForExpiry()` updates the engine index every 5 min but broadcasts nothing. MapView.tsx:143 renders `sigmets.features.filter((f) => f.geometry)` with no valid_to check.
failure_scenario: AWC fails or rate-limits for 2 h (FR-19 stale scenario). Every SIGMET that expires during that time stays drawn on connected browsers with active=true until the user reloads, while /status 'active' and the engine have already dropped it. Even in normal operation an expired polygon can stay for up to 5 minutes past valid_to. Users see hazards that are no longer valid, contrary to the data-honesty rule.

reason: Confirmed. WsHub sends SIGMETs only on SigmetsUpdated (:120-123) and in sendInitial (:97-105). SigmetGeoJson.collection (:17-27) filters `validTo > now` and sets `active` only at send time (:42). EngineService.rebuildForExpiry (:70-75) updates only the engine index. During an AWC outage it stays until the page reloads. /status and the engine have already dropped it, and the map contradicts them, which violates the data-honesty rule.

title: Region fallback to OpenSky drains the shared OpenSky budget in under an hour and bypasses the credit-reserve pause, killing the global view for the rest of the UTC day
evidence: config.py:25 `aircraft_providers: str = "adsb_lol,adsb_fi,opensky"` and opensky.py:19-21 `supports_region = True ... region_cost = 4`, so the region chain (main.py:97) falls back to OpenSky at 10 s cadence. config.py:42 `budget_opensky: int = 4000`, while global alone uses 720 × 4 = 2,880 per day. aircraft.py:100-106 sets `self._global_paused_until` on whichever job instance got the response, but the pause is only consulted when `need_global` (:38-42), so the region job ignores the reserve. Collector logs show adsb.lol 429 back-offs 7 times in 3 h.
failure_scenario: adsb.lol is rate-limited (observed) while adsb.fi fails 3 times (600 s cooldown). The region job switches to OpenSky and spends 4 credits about every 11 s, roughly 1,300 per hour. The remaining daily budget is exhausted in under an hour, after which both jobs get `budget_exhausted` and the world view is frozen or empty until 00:00 UTC. If OpenSky's reported remaining credits fall below the reserve during region calls, the region job keeps calling anyway.
fix: Keep OpenSky as a region provider only with its own capped sub-budget and a slower cadence (for example ≥ 60 s while on OpenSky), or drop it from the region default order. Make the reserve pause a property of the provider (shared by both chains) and check it in ProviderChain.pick for every scope.
reason: Confirmed in the code, with a narrower trigger than claimed. OpenSkyProvider has `supports_region = True`, `region_cost = 4` (opensky.py:19-21), and it is third in the default order (config.py:25). So when adsb_lol is in 429 backoff (observed live: `adsb_lol rate limited (429) — backing off 300 s` at 11:49 and 11:56) and adsb_fi is in its 600 s cooldown, the region job polls OpenSky every about 10 s: 360 calls/h × 4 = 1,440 budget units/h against `budget_opensky = 4000`/day (config.py:42). The reserve pause is broken for region: aircraft.py:100-106 sets `self._global_paused_until` on whichever instance saw the header, but the region instance never reads it (checked only under `need_global`, :38-42). The region job keeps spending below the reserve until `budget_exhausted`, after which both chains mark OpenSky down and global stops. "Under an hour" depends on the remaining budget and needs both ADS-B providers down at once for an extended period. pick() returns to adsb_lol as soon as its backoff expires, so short overlaps cost little. Currently budget:opensky has used=288 and region has never used OpenSky (0 log lines).
fix_v: Move the reserve pause into the provider or a shared object. Add `OpenSkyProvider.paused_until` set from `result.budget.remaining < settings.opensky_reserve_credits`, and have `ProviderChain.pick` skip a provider when `getattr(p, 'paused_until', None)` is in the future, for every scope. title: Shutdown order is the reverse of design 5.3: TrackWriter flushes before the consumer stops (ACKed rows are lost), there is no app-level going_away, and Docker's 10 s grace can cut the flush short
evidence: TrackWriter.java:64-65 does not override getPhase(), so it gets DEFAULT_PHASE = Integer.MAX_VALUE, and `stop() { running = false; flush(); }`. StreamConsumer.java:98 `getPhase() { return Integer.MAX_VALUE - 10; }`. Spring stops the highest phase first, so TrackWriter flushes while the consumer is still running. StreamConsumer.stop() (:89-92) only interrupts and does not join. No GOING_AWAY/1001 is sent anywhere (grep finds none), so WsHub has no lifecycle hook. The compose api service has no stop_grace_period (Docker default 10 s), while flush() alone may take `deadline = ... + 10_000` (:90).
failure_scenario: On `docker compose restart api`, TrackWriter drains its queue and stops its worker. The consumer keeps processing the next region snapshot(s) for up to about 10 s, enqueues about 110 rows each into a stopped writer, and ACKs them, so they are never written and never redelivered. The result is a track gap at every restart. If the flush plus Tomcat graceful shutdown exceeds 10 s, Docker SIGKILLs the JVM mid-flush. WS clients are dropped last instead of receiving going_away first.
fix: Give TrackWriter a lower phase than StreamConsumer (for example MAX−20) so it stops after the consumer, and join the consumer thread in StreamConsumer.stop(). Add a WsHub SmartLifecycle with phase MAX that closes all sessions with CloseStatus.GOING_AWAY first. Set `stop_grace_period: 30s` on the api service.
reason: Partially confirmed; one sub-claim is refuted. The claim "No GOING_AWAY/1001 is sent anywhere, WsHub has no lifecycle hook" is FALSE: WsHub implements SmartLifecycle (WsHub.java:43) with phase MAX-100 (:75), and stop() closes every session with `CloseStatus.GOING_AWAY.withReason("server shutting down")` (:77-85) before Tomcat's graceful shutdown. The ordering defect is real. TrackWriter does not override getPhase (default Integer.MAX_VALUE), so it stops first (`stop() { running = false; flush(); }`, :65), while StreamConsumer (phase MAX-10, :98) keeps consuming. Rows from snapshots processed during flush(), or after it drained the queue, are enqueued into a stopped writer (onSnapshot is not gated by `running`, :52-61) and then ACKed in handle()'s finally (StreamConsumer.java:173). They are lost, one region snapshot of about 110 rows or more per restart. StreamConsumer.stop() (:89-92) only interrupts and does not join. compose.yml has no stop_grace_period for api (Docker default 10 s), while flush() allows up to 10 s (:90), so a slow DB can get SIGKILLed mid-flush.
fix_v: Add `@Override public int getPhase() { return Integer.MAX_VALUE - 20; }` to TrackWriter, so it stops after StreamConsumer (MAX-10) and before WsHub (MAX-100). In StreamConsumer.stop(), after interrupt, `worker.join(Duration.ofSeconds(5))`. Add `stop_grace_period: 30s` to the api service in infra/compose.yml. Keep the existing WsHub going_away.

title: DB outage returns 500 instead of 503 + Retry-After, and the live aircraft-detail endpoint fails entirely because of an unguarded static-info lookup
evidence: ProblemAdvice.java:45-48 `@ExceptionHandler(Exception.class) ... log.error("unhandled error ...", e); return build(HttpStatus.INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, "INTERNAL", ...)`. There is no DataAccessException mapping, and `Problem.unavailable(...)` (Problem.java:22) is never used. AircraftController.java:87-88 `AircraftState a = snapshots.find(h); Map<String, Object> stat = aircraft.find(h);` makes an unguarded DB call on the live detail path. Design 5.1: "조회 API는 503 + Retry-After. 실시간 경로는 DB에 의존하지 않음".
failure_scenario: Postgres is down or saturated. Every history, track, replay, stats and airports request waits 5 s (Hikari connection-timeout), returns 500 INTERNAL and logs a full ERROR stack trace, and clients get no Retry-After hint. Clicking any aircraft on the live map also fails after 5 s, even though its state is in memory.
fix: Add `@ExceptionHandler({CannotGetJdbcConnectionException.class, DataAccessResourceFailureException.class, QueryTimeoutException.class})` returning 503 with `Retry-After: 30` and log it at WARN without the stack. In detail(), wrap aircraft.find in try/catch, return `static: null` with a meta note, and still serve the live state.
reason: Confirmed. ProblemAdvice.java:45-49 maps every unhandled exception, including Spring DataAccessException subclasses, to 500 INTERNAL with `log.error(..., e)` (full stack). Problem.unavailable (Problem.java:22) is never referenced (grep finds only its definition), and the only Retry-After in the codebase is in RateLimitFilter. Design 5.1 ("DB 종료·느림" row) requires "조회 API는 503 + Retry-After". AircraftController.detail (:84-100) calls `aircraft.find(h)` unguarded after the in-memory lookup. With the DB down, clicking a live aircraft waits about 5 s (Hikari connection-timeout 5000) and returns 500, although `snapshots.find(h)` has the state.
fix_v: Add to ProblemAdvice: `@ExceptionHandler({CannotGetJdbcConnectionException.class, DataAccessResourceFailureException.class, TransientDataAccessException.class}) ResponseEntity<ProblemDetail> dbUnavailable(Exception e, HttpServletRequest req)`. Log at WARN without the stack trace and return `build(HttpStatus.SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE, "UNAVAILABLE", "service unavailable", "history store unavailable", req)` with header `Retry-After: 30`. In AircraftController.detail: `Map<String,Object> stat; try { stat = aircraft.find(h); } catch (DataAccessException ex) { stat = null; m.put("static_unavailable", true); }` and return 404 only when `a == null` and the lookup succeeded with no row.

title: KMA radar budget limit is configured but never wired in, so calls are unlimited and the ops screen shows limit 0

reason: Confirmed, and the live data makes it worse than stated. main.py:66-73 `limits` has no "kma_radar" entry, so Budget.reserve uses limit 0, which the Lua script treats as unlimited (`if limit > 0 and ...`). (2) Fix the churn in kma_radar.py:88-91: `frames = await self._frames(); have = {f["tm"] for f in frames}; floor = frames[0]["tm"] if len(frames) >= KEEP_FRAMES else ""; candidates = [tm for tm in listing.data if floor < tm <= now_tm and tm not in have][-MAX_PER_CYCLE:]`. Steady state is then 1 listing plus 1 binary per cycle, about 576/day.

title: The 1-minute summary and daily stats jobs have no catch-up, so any api downtime at the scheduled minute leaves permanent gaps
evidence: MaintenanceJobs.java:55-66 `@Scheduled(cron = "0 5 * * * *")` summarises only `ts >= date_trunc('hour', now()) - interval '1 hour' AND ts < date_trunc('hour', now())`, the previous hour only. :75-76 `@Scheduled(cron = "0 30 3 * * *") aggregateDaily() { aggregate(LocalDate.now(ZoneOffset.UTC).minusDays(1)); }` covers yesterday only. Both writes are idempotent (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, or delete then insert) but never cover earlier windows.
failure_scenario: The api is restarting or down at 10:05 UTC (for example during `make bench`, which recreates it). Hour 09:00-10:00 is never summarised into track_point_1m. After the 72-hour raw retention, 30-day replay for that hour returns nothing. The same happens to a day's stats if the api is down at 03:30 UTC.
fix: Summarise the last N closed hours (for example 6) on every run, relying on ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING. Aggregate the last 3 days daily. Or record the last completed window in app_setting and backfill from there on startup.
reason: Confirmed in the code. summarize1m (MaintenanceJobs.java:55-73) covers only `[date_trunc('hour', now()) - 1h, date_trunc('hour', now()))`, and aggregateDaily (:75-76) covers only yesterday. Spring @Scheduled cron has no misfire catch-up, so if the api is down at hh:05:00 or 03:30:00 UTC that window is never processed. No gap exists yet: track_point_1m has hours 08, 09 and 10, and 11 is due at 12:05. The code path is certain, but it only triggers on downtime at those exact minutes. After the 72 h raw retention, the 30-day replay for a missed hour would be empty.
fix_v: Change the summary WHERE to the last 6 closed hours, `ts >= date_trunc('hour', now()) - interval '6 hours' AND ts < date_trunc('hour', now())`, which is safe with the existing `ON CONFLICT (hex, ts_minute) DO NOTHING`. Change aggregateDaily to loop over the last 3 days: `for (int i = 1; i <= 3; i++) aggregate(today.minusDays(i));`, which is idempotent through the delete then insert. Also call both once from an ApplicationReadyEvent handler (best-effort).

title: KMA radar frame list outlives its frame images, so the API reports available frames whose PNG URLs return 404

title: Health checks don't reflect ingestion: collector has no healthcheck, api readiness and /healthz stay UP while the consumer is stuck, and the design's trimmed-message metric is missing
evidence: compose.yml:90-118: the collector service has no `healthcheck:`, while Makefile:57,61 use `up -d --build --wait`. HealthController.java:22 always returns `"status", "ok"` regardless of region_lag_s. application.yml sets `endpoint.health.probes.enabled: true` with no readiness group includes, so readiness covers only readinessState and not redis, db or the consumer. publisher.py:55,60 use `maxlen=MAXLEN, approximate=True`, and nothing exports the trimmed-entry count required by design 5.2 ("잘린 건수는 지표로 노출").
failure_scenario: The collector crash-loops in `_connect_db`, or its jobs sit in 300 s backoff (REL-3). The stream consumer spins in its 3 s retry loop (for example a Redis auth or NOGROUP error), or falls behind and MAXLEN trims unread snapshots. `docker compose ps` and `--wait` still report every service Up or healthy, /healthz returns status ok, and there is no metric for lost stream entries. Add a custom api health indicator in a separate `ingest` health group (so readiness does not flap) that reports DOWN when region lag exceeds 120 s, and make /healthz status reflect it. Export XINFO GROUPS `lag` and `entries-read` as gauges (skywx_stream_lag, skywx_stream_trimmed_total).
reason: Confirmed. The compose collector service (infra/compose.yml:118-155) has no healthcheck, so `up --wait` (Makefile:57,61,68) treats it as ready once it is running. In the api, add an `IngestHealthIndicator` (DOWN when region lag exceeds 120 s) in a separate `management.endpoint.health.group.ingest.include=ingest` group, not readiness, and make /healthz return `status: degraded` from it. Export XINFO GROUPS `lag` for each stream as a gauge `skywx_stream_lag{stream}` from a @Scheduled(30 s) task.

title: Alert persistence starts a new unordered virtual thread per engine batch, so LEFT/CLEARED can run before the matching INSERT and leave the row open forever
evidence: AlertRepository.java:35-41 `@EventListener public void onAlerts(EngineEvents.AlertsChanged e) { Thread.ofVirtual().start(() -> { for (...) persist(ev); }); }` starts one thread per batch with no ordering between batches. :60-61 `UPDATE alert_event SET left_at = :left WHERE id = :id AND left_at IS NULL` is a no-op if the INSERT has not committed yet. Each ENTERED also first runs `sigmets.upsert(s)` (:49-50), which lengthens that thread.
failure_scenario: The DB is slow: Hikari waits for a connection with 12 pooled, while TrackWriter, touch() and REST compete. The batch with PREDICTED for key K (cycle N) is still waiting when cycle N+1's PREDICTION_CLEARED for K runs; its UPDATE matches 0 rows, and then the INSERT lands with left_at NULL. The alert appears open forever in history and is excluded from dwell statistics.
fix: Persist through a single ordered consumer, such as a single-thread executor or a bounded BlockingQueue drained by one virtual thread, preserving event order. Alternatively, make LEFT and CLEARED an upsert that records left_at even if it arrives first (`INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (hex, sigmet_id, kind, entered_at) DO UPDATE SET left_at = ...`).
reason: The race is confirmed in the code but was not observed. AlertRepository.onAlerts (:35-42) starts a new virtual thread per AlertsChanged batch with no ordering between batches. The LEFT/CLEARED UPDATE (:60-61) is a no-op if the INSERT from an earlier batch has not committed. Engine runs can be close together (a SigmetsUpdated right after a snapshot, or a global snapshot followed by a region one), and a first batch after a restart can hold hundreds of events, each preceded by `sigmets.upsert` (:49-50). Probe: every open alert_event row created since the 11:19:24 restart matches an active alert from GET /api/v1/alerts (0 stray open rows), so the race has not fired under the current healthy DB. It needs a slow or saturated DB (Hikari pool of 12, shared with TrackWriter, touch() and REST).
fix_v: Replace `Thread.ofVirtual().start(...)` per batch with a single ordered writer: a `LinkedBlockingQueue<AlertStateMachine.Event>` (bounded, for example 50,000, with an overflow counter) drained by one virtual thread started in a SmartLifecycle, calling persist(ev) in order. This also removes unbounded thread creation when the DB is slow.
