title: A WS subscribe spam flood is an unauthenticated ~14,000x amplification DoS (full snapshot, SIGMET GeoJSON and alerts serialized per message)
evidence: SkyWsHandler.java:75 `case "subscribe" -> subscribe(s, m);`. There is no per-session message rate or subscribe interval anywhere in the handler (only the 4 KB size limit at :44). :102 `hub.sendInitial(s, engine.activeAlerts(null));`. WsHub.java:52 `Executors.newVirtualThreadPerTaskExecutor()` (unbounded). :79-86 `pool.submit(() -> { sendFull(s); sendSigmets(s, sigmets.state()); sendRadar(...); s.sendOrDrop(toJson(Map.of("type","alerts",...))); sendStatus(s); })`. Serialization happens before any backpressure check: :170 `if (s.sendOrDrop(toJson(msg)))`, and :174 builds the whole SIGMET FeatureCollection before WsSession.java:53-55 looks at `out.isOpen()`/`getBufferSize()`. Measured on the running stack: one 80-byte `{"type":"subscribe","bbox":[-180,-90,180,90],"zoom":3,"detail":"lite"}` returned 1,136,081 bytes (snapshot 838,430 + alerts 186,049 + sigmets 108,937 + status/radar).
failure_scenario: A script, or a web page via DNS rebinding (SEC-7), opens the 5 allowed sockets, reads fast, and sends subscribe in a tight loop. Each 80-byte message spawns a virtual thread that builds and serializes about 1.1 MB (~8,800 aircraft plus 125 polygons plus all alerts). Thousands of messages per second saturate CPU and fill the ~600 MB heap (1 GB container, MaxRAMPercentage=60). ExitOnOutOfMemoryError then restarts the api: every WS client drops and the in-memory snapshot is lost. Tasks already queued keep serializing after the socket closes, because sendFull only checks `s.bbox == null`.
fix: Add a per-session token bucket in handleTextMessage (for example ≤1 subscribe/s and ≤10 messages/s; close with 1008 on repeated violation). Coalesce initial sends with a per-session `AtomicBoolean initialPending` so a new subscribe replaces an in-flight one instead of queuing another. Check `out.isOpen()` and the buffer size before serializing. Cache the serialized SIGMET collection and alerts payload per version (serialize once, share the String). Bound concurrent initial sends with a Semaphore. At the edge, add `limit_req` on the /ws/ handshake.
reason: Confirmed in code. SkyWsHandler.java:75 dispatches every `subscribe` to subscribe(), and :102 calls `hub.sendInitial(s, engine.activeAlerts(null))` with no per-session rate limit or coalescing. The only guard is the 4 KB frame limit (:44). activeAlerts (EngineService.java:117-124) copies every active alert under the engine `synchronized (lock)` on the handler thread for each message, which also contends with the engine cycle. WsHub.java:52 uses an unbounded virtual-thread executor. :97-104 submits one task per subscribe that serializes the full snapshot (:173-188), the whole SIGMET FeatureCollection (:191-193), all alerts (:102) and status. Serialization happens before WsSession.sendOrDrop checks `out.isOpen()`/buffer (WsSession.java:53-55), and sendFull only checks `s.bbox == null`, which is never cleared on close. Queued tasks therefore keep serializing after a 1008 close. ConcurrentWebSocketSessionDecorator's DROP strategy discards the extra copies, but only after the CPU and allocation cost is paid. Payload scale verified via REST: /api/v1/alerts = 206,934 B and /api/v1/sigmets = 106,530 B. Together with the ~7,300-aircraft snapshot this is consistent with the reported ~1.1 MB per 80-byte message. The design's DoS row (WS 200 connections, 5 per IP) is bypassed by one connection. CPU saturation is certain. OOM depends on backlog growth and was not reproduced (no load test allowed).
fix_v: In WsSession add `final AtomicBoolean initialPending` and a small token bucket (for example 20 messages per 10 s). In SkyWsHandler.handleTextMessage, close with `CloseStatus.POLICY_VIOLATION.withReason("rate limit")` when the bucket is empty. In subscribe(), update s.bbox/zoom/detail but call hub.sendInitial only if `s.initialPending.compareAndSet(false, true)`. In the task, `s.initialPending.set(false)` first (so it serializes the latest bbox), and fetch alerts inside the task rather than on the handler thread. Add `if (!s.out.isOpen()) return;` at the top of sendFull/sendSigmets/sendInitial before any toJson. Cache the serialized `sigmets` payload per SigmetStore version and the alerts payload per alert-set version, as one shared String instead of per-session serialization. Optionally bound concurrent initial sends with a Semaphore (e.g. 8). At the edge, add `limit_req zone=perip burst=10 nodelay;` to `location /ws/` to throttle handshake churn.

title: The running api holds the DB owner (skywx_migrator) password, so 'api is DML-only / audit_log is INSERT-only' is not enforced
evidence: On the running stack, `docker compose exec api env` (names only) shows DB_MIGRATOR_PASSWORD. HEAD application.yml has `flyway: enabled: true, user: skywx_migrator, password: ${DB_MIGRATOR_PASSWORD:}`. 01-roles.sh:8 `CREATE DATABASE skywx OWNER skywx_migrator`, so the migrator can UPDATE/DELETE audit_log and DROP anything. Note: the working tree has an uncommitted, undeployed change (compose.yml:51-71 `migrate` one-shot service; application.yml `flyway.enabled: false`). Residual problem in that change: the migrate service still gets `DB_API_PASSWORD` and `REDIS_PASSWORD` (compose.yml:63,66), which a Flyway run should not need.
failure_scenario: Any code execution, SSRF-to-JDBC or deserialization bug in the api (see SEC-5) reads the env and connects as skywx_migrator. It can then `DELETE FROM audit_log` or `ALTER TABLE ... DISABLE TRIGGER`, erasing the operator trail that design 6.1 (Repudiation/EoP) says only an INSERT-only role can touch.
fix: Finish and deploy the one-shot migrate service. Give it only DB_MIGRATOR_PASSWORD and disable Redis/session autoconfig in the `migrate` profile so it does not need REDIS_PASSWORD or DB_API_PASSWORD. Add an integration test that connects as skywx_api and asserts `DELETE FROM audit_log` / `CREATE TABLE` fail with 42501.
reason: Confirmed for the running deployment: `docker compose exec api env` (names only) includes DB_MIGRATOR_PASSWORD, and skywx_migrator owns database skywx (`pg_get_userbyid(datdba)` = skywx_migrator; 01-roles.sh:8). So the api process holds credentials that can DELETE audit_log or DROP any table, defeating V1__init.sql:163 `GRANT INSERT, SELECT ON audit_log TO skywx_api`. The uncommitted working tree already fixes this. application.yml:19 has `flyway.enabled: false`, compose.yml:51-71 adds a one-shot `migrate` service, and the api service no longer receives DB_MIGRATOR_PASSWORD (compose.yml:78-94). The residual the auditor points to (migrate gets DB_API_PASSWORD at :63 and REDIS_PASSWORD at :66) is not material. It is a short-lived container running trusted code, and skywx_api is strictly less privileged than the migrator it already holds. I also checked the untracked V2 migration: SECURITY DEFINER with `SET search_path = public, pg_temp` and EXECUTE revoked from PUBLIC, so it adds no escalation path.
fix_v: Deploy the working-tree change (migrate service plus flyway disabled in the api) and verify `docker compose exec api env | cut -d= -f1` no longer lists DB_MIGRATOR_PASSWORD. Add an integration test that connects as skywx_api and asserts `DELETE FROM audit_log`, `UPDATE audit_log` and `CREATE TABLE x()` fail with SQLSTATE 42501. Optionally drop REDIS_PASSWORD/DB_API_PASSWORD from `migrate` if the `migrate` profile boots without them (exclude RedisAutoConfiguration/session autoconfig in that profile). This is low priority.

title: The edge, redis and db containers run as root with full default capabilities, writable rootfs and no no-new-privileges
evidence: compose.yml:13-30 (edge), :142-155 (redis) and :157-175 (db) do not use `<<: *hardened` (defined at :6-10 and applied only to web/api/collector/migrate). `docker inspect` on the running stack: `edge ro=false capdrop=[] secopt=[] user= image=nginx:1.27-alpine`, `redis ro=false capdrop=[] secopt=[] user=`, `db ro=false capdrop=[] secopt=[] user=`. None of edge/redis/db/web has a memory or pids limit. Design 6.1 (Elevation) requires non-root, read-only root FS and cap_drop ALL.
failure_scenario: The edge is the only process that parses raw attacker bytes. A memory-corruption bug in nginx 1.27.5 (not scanned, see SEC-8) yields code execution in a root master process with CAP_NET_RAW/CAP_SETUID/CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE and a writable filesystem. From there it can craft raw packets on the 10.77.0.0/24 bridge to talk to redis/db, drop persistent binaries, or escalate from a worker via setuid binaries, because no-new-privileges is absent. A redis or db compromise has the same unconstrained footprint.
fix: Edge: use `nginxinc/nginx-unprivileged` (listens on 8700 already, pid in /tmp) with `user: "101"`, `read_only: true`, `tmpfs: [/tmp, /var/cache/nginx]`, `cap_drop: [ALL]`, `security_opt: [no-new-privileges:true]` and mem/pids limits. Redis: `user: "999:1000"`, `read_only: true` (data on the volume), cap_drop ALL, no-new-privileges. DB: cap_drop ALL plus cap_add [CHOWN, DAC_OVERRIDE, FOWNER, SETUID, SETGID] (needed by the entrypoint), no-new-privileges, `tmpfs: [/var/run/postgresql, /tmp]`, mem limit.
reason: Partly refuted. The gap exists: docker inspect shows edge/redis/db with ReadonlyRootfs=false, CapDrop=[], SecurityOpt=[], no memory or pids limits, and they do not use `<<: *hardened` (compose.yml:13-30, 157-170, 172-190), contrary to design 6.1 Elevation (비root, read-only 루트 FS, cap_drop ALL). The failure scenario is overstated, though. Per /proc: nginx workers, which parse client bytes, run as uid 101 with CapEff=0. redis-server runs as uid 999 with CapEff=0. All postgres processes run as uid 999 with CapEff=0 (the entrypoints drop privileges). Only the nginx master is uid 0 with default caps, and it does not parse requests. The edge image has no setuid binaries (`find / -perm -4000` is empty), so the 'escalate from a worker via setuid' path does not exist there. The db image has setuid su/mount/passwd, but db is reachable only from the internal bridge. The edge is bound to 127.0.0.1. What remains is a missing defence-in-depth control the design promises.
fix_v: Edge: add `read_only: true`, `tmpfs: ["/tmp", "/var/cache/nginx", "/var/run"]`, `cap_drop: [ALL]`, `cap_add: [CHOWN, SETUID, SETGID]` (master drops to the nginx user), `security_opt: ["no-new-privileges:true"]`, `deploy.resources.limits: {memory: 128m, pids: 256}`. nginx.conf already puts the pid in /tmp. Alternatively switch to nginxinc/nginx-unprivileged with `user: "101"` and cap_drop ALL with no cap_add. Redis: `read_only: true`, `cap_drop: [ALL]`, `cap_add: [SETUID, SETGID]` (entrypoint gosu), no-new-privileges, mem limit ~320m. Data is already on the redis_data volume. DB: `cap_drop: [ALL]`, `cap_add: [CHOWN, DAC_OVERRIDE, FOWNER, SETUID, SETGID]`, no-new-privileges, `tmpfs: [/var/run/postgresql, /tmp]`, mem limit. Verify each with `docker compose up --wait`.

title: Redis uses one shared all-powerful 'default' user for api and collector, and ops sessions are JDK-serialized, so a collector compromise can forge ops sessions or trigger deserialization in the api
evidence: redis.conf defines no ACL users. `ACL USERS` on the running Redis returns only `default`. compose.yml:144 `--requirepass ${REDIS_PASSWORD}`, and api, collector and migrate all receive that same password. application.yml `session: redis.namespace: skywx:session`. No springSessionDefaultRedisSerializer bean exists anywhere, and OpsUserService.java:22-23 states `/** 세션(Redis, JDK 직렬화)에 저장되므로 Serializable. */`. redis.conf renames only FLUSHALL/FLUSHDB/CONFIG/DEBUG/SHUTDOWN, and `COMMAND INFO REPLICAOF` still resolves (MIGRATE/ACL/KEYS/SCRIPT also remain).
failure_scenario: The collector processes untrusted provider data. If it is compromised, it can HSET `skywx:session:sessions:<id>` with `sessionAttr:SPRING_SECURITY_CONTEXT` = a JDK-serialized SecurityContextImpl(OpsAuthentication, ROLE_OPS) and send `Cookie: SKYWX_SESSION=<base64 id>`. That gives full ops access (settings, provider disable, audit read) without a password. It could instead plant a gadget chain that the api deserializes on session load. It can also rewrite `skywx:settings`, reset `rl:*` counters, or `REPLICAOF` to an attacker host, which wipes every stream, budget and session.
fix: Create per-service Redis ACL users and disable `default`. collector: `~skywx:aircraft ~skywx:sigmet ~skywx:radar ~skywx:budget:* ~skywx:provider:* ~skywx:active ~skywx:collector ~skywx:events ~skywx:radar_kr:* %R~skywx:settings -@all +@read +@write +@stream +eval +evalsha -@dangerous`. api: its own key patterns including skywx:session:* and rl:*. Switch Spring Session to a JSON serializer with an allow-list, or store only user id and role and reload from DB. Rename or disable REPLICAOF/SLAVEOF/MIGRATE/ACL/MODULE in redis.conf.
reason: Confirmed. Read-only probe from the collector (using its own REDIS_PASSWORD): `ACL USERS` → [b'default'], and `ACL WHOAMI` → default. api and collector share this all-powerful user. redis.conf:11-16 renames only FLUSHALL/FLUSHDB/CONFIG/DEBUG/SHUTDOWN, and COMMAND INFO still resolves REPLICAOF, SLAVEOF, MIGRATE, MODULE, KEYS, SCRIPT and ACL. There is no springSessionDefaultRedisSerializer bean in the api (grep finds nothing; RedisConfig.java only defines stream beans). OpsUserService.java:22 says `세션(Redis, JDK 직렬화)`, so the SecurityContextImpl(OpsAuthentication with ROLE_OPS) is JDK-serialized. The security chain trusts it via HttpSessionSecurityContextRepository (SecurityConfig.java:103-106) with no DB re-check. A compromised collector, which parses third-party payloads, can therefore write `skywx:session:sessions:<id>` with a forged context and obtain ops access, or REPLICAOF the instance away. The precondition (collector compromise) is the same as SEC-1.
fix_v: Add an ACL file (mount it read-only and set `aclfile /etc/redis/users.acl`) with hashed passwords, and switch each client to username+password. Suggested lines: `user default off`. `user collector on #<sha256> ~skywx:aircraft ~skywx:sigmet ~skywx:radar ~skywx:radar_kr:* ~skywx:events ~skywx:collector ~skywx:active ~skywx:provider:* ~budget:* %R~skywx:settings resetchannels -@all +@read +@write +@stream +@hash +@string +@scripting +@connection -@dangerous`. `user api on #<sha256> ~skywx:* ~rl:* ~budget:* resetchannels +@all -@dangerous`. The key list comes from grep of collector/api (budget.py:25 `budget:{provider}:{d}`, status.py:28, etc.). Validate against `ACL LOG` in the fixture stack. Set spring.data.redis.username=api and the collector's redis username=collector. As defence in depth, add a JVM serial filter to the api (`-Djdk.serialFilter=dev.skywx.**;org.springframework.security.**;org.springframework.session.**;java.**;!*`) or store only ops_user_id in the session and rebuild the Authentication from ops_user per request.

title: The 5-failures/15-min login lockout can be bypassed by concurrent attempts; the login limiter fails open and failed logins are never audited
evidence: OpsUserService.java:34 reads `failed_count` with a plain SELECT (no FOR UPDATE, no @Transactional). :46 `int failed = ((Number) r.get("failed_count")).intValue() + 1;` :50 `UPDATE ops_user SET failed_count = :f WHERE id = :id` writes an absolute value (lost update). :44 `if (lockedUntil != null && lockedUntil.isAfter(Instant.now())) return Optional.empty();` returns before the ~250 ms BCrypt(12), creating a timing oracle. OpsSessionController.java:53 `if (limiter.hit("login", ip, 60)[0] > 10)`. RateLimiter.java:34-35 `catch (RuntimeException e) { return new long[]{0, windowS}; }` fails open for the login bucket too. Only success is audited (:64 `audit.record(req, user.id(), "LOGIN", ...)`).
failure_scenario: An attacker sends 10 concurrent wrong-password POSTs per minute (the per-IP cap). All 10 read failed_count=k during BCrypt and all write k+1, so the lock triggers only after about 50 guesses instead of 5. The fast responses reveal exactly when the lock expires, so the next batch is timed precisely. While Redis is unavailable the 10/min limit disappears as well. Behind Docker Desktop every client arrives as 10.77.0.1, so the 'per-IP' login bucket is global: the same actor also blocks the real operator's logins. None of this appears in audit_log or on the ops audit tab.
fix: Do the failure bookkeeping in one statement: `UPDATE ops_user SET failed_count = failed_count + 1, locked_until = CASE WHEN failed_count + 1 >= 5 THEN now() + interval '15 minutes' ELSE locked_until END WHERE id = :id RETURNING failed_count, locked_until` (reset failed_count when locking), or SELECT ... FOR UPDATE inside @Transactional. Always run a BCrypt compare, even when locked. Make the login bucket fail closed (503) when Redis errors. Insert audit rows for LOGIN_FAILED and ACCOUNT_LOCKED (target = username, user_id nullable).
reason: Code confirmed. OpsUserService.authenticate has no @Transactional. :34 is a plain SELECT, :46 computes `failed_count + 1` in Java, and :50 writes the absolute value `SET failed_count = :f`. N concurrent wrong-password requests that read the same k all write k+1, so with the 10/min login bucket (OpsSessionController.java:53) the 5-failure lock needs about 50 guesses instead of 5. :44 returns before BCrypt when locked (fast-path timing). RateLimiter.java:34-35 returns {0, window} on any Redis error (fails open). Only successful LOGIN is audited (:64). Severity is lowered from medium: the admin password is strong (checked by length/classes only: 24 chars, 4 classes), `make ops-user` enforces ≥12 chars, and BCrypt(12) caps concurrent guesses, so the 10x weakening has no practical brute-force impact. With Redis down, the DB lockout still applies and sessions cannot be saved. Missing audit rows for failed or locked logins are a legitimate gap. audit_log.user_id is nullable (V1__init.sql:149), so they can be recorded.
fix_v: Replace :46-51 with one atomic statement: `UPDATE ops_user SET failed_count = CASE WHEN failed_count + 1 >= :max THEN 0 ELSE failed_count + 1 END, locked_until = CASE WHEN failed_count + 1 >= :max THEN now() + make_interval(mins => :m) ELSE locked_until END WHERE id = :id RETURNING locked_until`. When the row is locked, still run `encoder.matches(password, DUMMY_HASH)` before returning. In OpsSessionController, make the login bucket fail closed: add a RateLimiter method that rethrows, and map it to 503. Call `audit.record(req, null, "LOGIN_FAILED", username, null, null)` on failure and `"ACCOUNT_LOCKED"` when the UPDATE returns a new locked_until.

title: No Host allow-list at edge or Origin allow-list for WS, so DNS rebinding turns the 127.0.0.1-only service into one any website can drive
evidence: nginx.conf:37-38 `listen 8700; server_name _;` is the only server and accepts any Host. proxy_headers.conf:3 `proxy_set_header Host $http_host;` forwards the client's Host. WebSocketConfig.java:33 `registry.addHandler(handler, "/ws/v1")` has no `setAllowedOrigins`, so Spring's check compares Origin against that attacker-chosen Host. Probe: `curl -H 'Host: rebind.attacker.example:8700' http://localhost:8700/api/v1/status` → 200, and /api/v1/openapi reflects `servers: [{'url': 'http://rebind.attacker.example:8700'}]`. The edge logs every client as 10.77.0.1, so all per-IP limits are shared.
failure_scenario: The operator visits http://rebind.attacker.example:8700; its DNS then flips to 127.0.0.1. The page's JavaScript is now same-origin with SkyWx: Origin http://rebind.attacker.example:8700 equals Host, so the WS handshake passes. It can run the SEC-2 subscribe flood to crash the api, use up the shared 5 WS slots and 120/min API budget, or POST /api/v1/ops/session (CSRF-exempt when no session cookie is present) to keep the admin account locked out or brute-force it (SEC-6).
fix: In nginx, add `server { listen 8700 default_server; return 444; }` and serve the app only from `server { listen 8700; server_name localhost 127.0.0.1; ... }` (port-aware for the 8701 E2E stack). In the api, call `setAllowedOrigins(props.allowedOrigins())` (e.g. http://localhost:8700, http://127.0.0.1:8700) instead of relying on a Host-derived same-origin check, and reject requests whose Host is not in the list.
reason: Confirmed. nginx.conf:37-38 has one catch-all server (`listen 8700; server_name _;`), and proxy_headers.conf:3 forwards `Host $http_host`. Probe: `curl -H 'Host: rebind.attacker.example:8700' http://localhost:8700/api/v1/status` → 200. WebSocketConfig.java:33 registers `/ws/v1` without setAllowedOrigins/setAllowedOriginPatterns, so Spring's default same-origin check compares Origin to the attacker-controlled Host and passes after a DNS rebind. Edge logs show every client as 10.77.0.1, so the per-IP login, API and WS budgets are effectively global. Impact is limited to availability: the rebinding origin has no SKYWX_SESSION cookie (it is scoped to localhost), so ops actions are impossible. A rebinding page can drive the SEC-2 subscribe flood, use up the 5 shared WS slots or the 120/min budget, and lock the admin account with 5 failed logins (login is CSRF-exempt without a session cookie, SecurityConfig.java:43). Browser local-network-access protections may reduce reachability in some browsers; this was not verified.
fix_v: nginx: add `server { listen 8700 default_server; return 444; }` and change the app server to `server_name localhost 127.0.0.1;`. server_name ignores the port, so the 8701 E2E stack and the `wget http://127.0.0.1:8700/healthz` healthcheck keep working. api: in WebSocketConfig use `registry.addHandler(handler, "/ws/v1").setAllowedOriginPatterns("http://localhost:[*]", "http://127.0.0.1:[*]")`, ideally driven by an AppProperties list for deployments. Optionally add a OncePerRequestFilter that rejects Host values outside the same list with 421.

title: The CI Trivy step scans image names that don't exist; pip-audit, Dependabot and scans of third-party images are missing
evidence: ci.yml:62 builds through compose, which tags images `skywx-api:local`, `skywx-collector:local`, `skywx-web:local` (compose.yml:33,74,113). ci.yml:64/66/68 scan `image-ref: skywx-api` / `skywx-collector` / `skywx-web`, which resolve to `:latest`: not present locally, so Trivy falls back to a registry pull and exits with a fatal error. The only dependency audit is `npm audit` (ci.yml:40): no pip-audit/uv audit for the collector and no Gradle dependency check. .github contains only workflows/, with no dependabot.yml. nginx:1.27-alpine, redis:8-alpine and imresamu/postgis:18-3.6 (compose.yml:14,143,158) and grafana/k6:latest (Makefile:70-71, attached to the internal network) are never scanned and not digest-pinned. Design 6.2/NFR-10 require Trivy, npm/pip audit and weekly Dependabot.
failure_scenario: The security job either always fails, so it is ignored and becomes noise, or is 'fixed' by relaxing exit codes. Either way, a HIGH/CRITICAL CVE in the collector's Pillow/numpy/shapely or in the internet-facing nginx image ships without any signal, and a moved `latest` tag silently changes what runs next to redis and db.
fix: Use `image-ref: skywx-api:local` (etc.) and add Trivy jobs for the nginx/redis/postgis images. Pin all images by digest. Add `uvx pip-audit` (on `uv export --no-dev` output) and a Gradle dependency-check or `trivy fs apps/api`. Add .github/dependabot.yml (npm, uv/pip, gradle, docker, github-actions; weekly). Pin third-party actions by commit SHA.
reason: Confirmed. ci.yml:62 builds via compose, whose images are tagged `skywx-api:local`, `skywx-collector:local` and `skywx-web:local` (compose.yml:33, 53, 74, 113). ci.yml:64/66/68 scan `image-ref: skywx-api` etc., which default to `:latest`. That tag does not exist locally, so Trivy falls back to a registry lookup of docker.io/library/skywx-api:latest and fails, and no image is actually scanned. The only dependency audit is `npm audit` (ci.yml:40): there is no pip-audit/uv audit for the collector and no Gradle dependency scan. .github contains only workflows/ (no dependabot.yml). nginx:1.27-alpine, redis:8-alpine and imresamu/postgis:18-3.6 are not scanned or digest-pinned, and Makefile:70-71 runs grafana/k6:latest on the internal network. Design NFR-10 and 6.2 CI require Trivy (images), npm/pip audit and weekly Dependabot.
fix_v: ci.yml: change the image refs to `skywx-api:local`, `skywx-collector:local` and `skywx-web:local`. Add Trivy steps for `nginx:1.27-alpine`, `redis:8-alpine` and `imresamu/postgis:18-3.6`, pinning each by digest in compose. In the collector job add `uv export --no-dev --format requirements-txt -o /tmp/req.txt && uvx pip-audit -r /tmp/req.txt --strict`. Add `aquasecurity/trivy-action` with `scan-type: fs, scan-ref: apps/api` (or OWASP dependency-check) for Gradle. Add .github/dependabot.yml with weekly updates for npm (/apps/web), pip/uv (/apps/collector), gradle (/apps/api), docker (/apps/api, /apps/web, /apps/collector) and github-actions (/). Pin k6 to a version tag in the Makefile.

title: The public OpenAPI document lists every ops endpoint, and anonymous POSTs get a distinctive 403, defeating the 'unauthorized ops paths return 404' hiding
evidence: application.yml:50-51 `springdoc: api-docs.path: /api/v1/openapi` (only swagger-ui is disabled). SecurityConfig.java:39 `.anyRequest().permitAll()`. Probe: GET /api/v1/openapi → 200, and its paths include /api/v1/ops/settings/{key}, /api/v1/ops/providers/{name}/{action}, /api/v1/ops/audit, /api/v1/ops/dlq, /api/v1/ops/stats/aggregate. SecurityConfig.java:41-43: CSRF is evaluated before authorization, so an anonymous `POST /api/v1/ops/doesnotexist` returns 403 `CSRF_INVALID`, while GETs return 404.
failure_scenario: An anonymous client downloads the complete ops attack surface (paths, parameters, body shapes) and confirms the /api/v1/ops namespace exists. This contradicts design 6.1's '비인가 ops 경로는 404'.
fix: Set `springdoc.api-docs.enabled: false` by default (enable it only in a dev profile), or exclude `/api/v1/ops/**` with GroupedOpenApi.pathsToExclude and require ROLE_OPS for /api/v1/openapi. In accessDeniedHandler, return the 404 problem for CsrfException when the request is unauthenticated.
reason: The evidence is accurate, but the claimed harm is not material. GET /api/v1/openapi → 200 with 10 /api/v1/ops/* paths. An anonymous POST to /api/v1/ops/doesnotexist → 403 CSRF_INVALID, and a GET → 404. However, the design itself publishes the ops endpoint list: the §9.3 API table lists every /ops endpoint, and §9.4 says the springdoc OpenAPI snapshot is committed to the repository. So hiding it at runtime protects nothing in a portfolio repo. The POST 403 is returned identically for existing and nonexistent ops paths, so it does not reveal whether any particular endpoint exists. FR-14 explicitly specifies 'CSRF 없는 변경 요청 → 403'. No concrete failure scenario beyond information the project already publishes.
fix_v: No change required. If desired for consistency with NFR-11, exclude /api/v1/ops/** from the generated docs via `GroupedOpenApi.builder().pathsToExclude("/api/v1/ops/**")`.

title: Spring MVC 4xx errors (405/415/406) are turned into 500s plus ERROR-level stack traces, an unauthenticated log-flooding vector
evidence: ProblemAdvice.java:45-49 `@ExceptionHandler(Exception.class) ... log.error("unhandled error request_id={} path={}", ..., e); return build(HttpStatus.INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, ...)`. There are no handlers for HttpRequestMethodNotSupportedException, HttpMediaTypeNotSupportedException or HttpMediaTypeNotAcceptableException. Probe: `curl -X DELETE /api/v1/status` → 500 `INTERNAL`, and the api log shows `ERROR ... ProblemAdvice : unhandled error` followed by `HttpRequestMethodNotSupportedException: Request method 'DELETE' is not supported` and a full stack. `POST -H 'Content-Type: text/plain' /api/v1/status` → 500.
failure_scenario: Any anonymous client at the edge limit (10 r/s) produces hundreds of stack-trace lines per second in api logs. Real errors are buried, disk fills, and 5xx-rate alerting fires falsely. Clients also get 500 instead of 405/415.
fix: Before the catch-all, handle `org.springframework.web.ErrorResponse`: `if (e instanceof ErrorResponse er) return build(HttpStatus.valueOf(er.getStatusCode().value()), ...)`, logging at DEBUG. Alternatively extend ResponseEntityExceptionHandler. Keep log.error only for genuine 5xx.
reason: Reproduced. `curl -X DELETE http://localhost:8700/api/v1/status` → 500 `INTERNAL`. The api log shows `ERROR ... ProblemAdvice : unhandled error request_id=... path=/api/v1/status` followed by `HttpRequestMethodNotSupportedException: Request method 'DELETE' is not supported` and a full stack trace. The cause is the catch-all at ProblemAdvice.java:45-49, which has no handler for Spring MVC's ErrorResponse exceptions (405/406/415). Volume is bounded by RateLimitFilter to 120/min for the effectively shared client IP 10.77.0.1, so about 2 stack traces per second. That still means wrong status codes, polluted 5xx metrics and noisy ERROR logs.
fix_v: At the top of ProblemAdvice.other(): `if (e instanceof org.springframework.web.ErrorResponse er && er.getStatusCode().is4xxClientError()) { log.debug("client error {} {}", er.getStatusCode(), req.getRequestURI()); var r = build(HttpStatus.valueOf(er.getStatusCode().value()), HttpStatus.valueOf(er.getStatusCode().value()).name(), "client error", "request not supported", req); return ResponseEntity.status(r.getStatusCode()).headers(er.getHeaders()).header("Content-Type","application/problem+json").body(r.getBody()); }`. Copying er.getHeaders() keeps the `Allow` header on 405. Keep log.error only for the remaining 5xx.

title: Ops changes and their audit records are not atomic, so a change can take effect with no audit row
evidence: OpsController.java:78 `redis.opsForHash().put(key, "disabled", disable ? "1" : "0");` then :79 `audit.record(...)`. :131 `settings.update(key, value, version, auth.getName());` (commits the UPDATE and mirrors to Redis) then :132 `audit.record(req, userId(auth), "SETTING_UPDATE", ...)`. These are separate statements with no @Transactional, and AuditService.record is an independent INSERT.
failure_scenario: Suppose the DB hiccups or Hikari's 12 connections are exhausted (5 s timeout) right after the Redis write or the settings commit. The provider is actually disabled, or the poll interval actually changed, and the collector applies it. The audit INSERT then throws, the operator sees a 500 and no audit_log row exists. That is exactly the repudiation gap audit_log is meant to close.
fix: For settings: put the UPDATE and the audit INSERT in one @Transactional method and mirror to Redis in a TransactionSynchronization afterCommit. For provider toggles: persist the disabled flag in the DB (app_setting) and audit it in the same transaction, then mirror to Redis after commit, or write the audit row first and compensate on Redis failure.
reason: Confirmed. OpsController.java:78 `redis.opsForHash().put(key, "disabled", ...)` runs before :79 `audit.record(...)`, and :131 `settings.update(...)` runs before :132 `audit.record(...)`. SettingsService.update (:46-50) commits the UPDATE (autocommit, no @Transactional) and mirrors to Redis before returning. AuditService.record (:24-31) is an independent INSERT. A concrete reachable case: with the DB unavailable or Hikari exhausted (12 connections, 5 s timeout), a provider toggle still succeeds in Redis (the session lives in Redis, so auth works), then the audit INSERT throws. The collector applies the change, the operator gets a 500, and no audit_log row exists. This violates design 6.3-4 ('모든 ops 변경은 audit_log 에 기록').

If the Redis write then fails, record a compensating `PROVIDER_TOGGLE_FAILED` row. putSetting: put the UPDATE and the audit INSERT in one @Transactional service method (e.g. SettingsService.updateAudited(key, value, version, userId, req)), and move mirror() into `TransactionSynchronizationManager.registerSynchronization(... afterCommit -> mirror())`.

title: The WS connection-limit check is check-then-act and not atomic, so concurrent handshakes exceed the per-IP and global caps
evidence: SkyWsHandler.java:46 `if (hub.count() >= props.wsMaxConn() || hub.countByIp(ip) >= props.wsMaxConnPerIp()) {` ... :51-52 `byId.put(raw.getId(), s); hub.add(s);`. afterConnectionEstablished runs concurrently per connection, and WsHub.countByIp (:73) scans a ConcurrentHashMap without reservation. The check runs only after the 101 upgrade.
failure_scenario: 10 simultaneous handshakes from one client (nginx limit_conn allows 10) all see countByIp=0 and are all admitted, so 10 sessions exist against the WS_MAX_CONN_PER_IP=5 limit. After an api restart, reconnect storms overshoot WS_MAX_CONN=200. Each admitted session receives a full ~1.1 MB initial payload (SEC-2), causing a memory spike.
fix: Reserve slots atomically: a global AtomicInteger and a ConcurrentHashMap<String, AtomicInteger> per IP, using incrementAndGet and then compare (decrement on reject or close). Enforce this in HandshakeInterceptor.beforeHandshake (return false with 429/503) so over-limit clients never complete the upgrade.
reason: Confirmed. SkyWsHandler.java:46 checks `hub.count()` and `hub.countByIp(ip)` (WsHub.java:90-91, a stream count over a ConcurrentHashMap), then :51-52 adds the session, with no atomic reservation. afterConnectionEstablished runs per connection on separate threads, so simultaneous handshakes can all pass. The check runs after the 101 upgrade. Impact is small: nginx `limit_conn perip_conn 10` (nginx.conf:62) caps the overshoot at 10 per IP instead of 5, and the global 200 cap overshoots only by the concurrency of a reconnect burst. Each extra admitted session can still trigger a full initial payload (see SEC-2).
fix_v: In WsHub keep `AtomicInteger total` and `ConcurrentHashMap<String, AtomicInteger> perIp`. Reserve in the HandshakeInterceptor.beforeHandshake (WebSocketConfig.java:35): `if (total.incrementAndGet() > max || perIp.computeIfAbsent(ip, k -> new AtomicInteger()).incrementAndGet() > maxPerIp) { rollback both; response.setStatusCode(HttpStatus.SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE); return false; }` and set attribute `skywx.reserved=true`. Release in afterConnectionClosed only when that attribute is set. Remove the post-upgrade check at SkyWsHandler.java:46.

title: KMA radar gzip is decompressed without a limit, bypassing the 20 MB response cap (decompression bomb takes down the whole collector)
evidence: kma_grid.py:106 `raw = gzip.decompress(gz_bytes)`. http.py:78-81 caps only the downloaded (compressed) bytes: `if size > settings.http_max_bytes: raise ResponseTooLarge`. The collector's memory limit is 512m (compose.yml:138).
failure_scenario: A corrupted or tampered HSR file under 20 MB inflates to several GB, and the collector is OOM-killed. The same frame is retried every cycle, so the collector restart-loops and aircraft/SIGMET collection stops too, not just radar.
fix: Decompress with `zlib.decompressobj(16 + zlib.MAX_WBITS)` using `max_length` = HEADER_BYTES + expected nx*ny*2 plus a margin (e.g. ≤ 64 MB). Raise ResponseTooLarge if `unconsumed_tail` remains, and record it as a quality/ingest error.
reason: Confirmed. kma_grid.py:106 `raw = gzip.decompress(gz_bytes)` is unbounded. http.py:78-81 caps only the transferred bytes (20 MB), and the HSR file is a gzip payload, not Content-Encoding, so httpx does not decode it. jobs/kma_radar.py:137-141 saves the raw file and then calls read_echo synchronously on the event loop. The frame is added to `have` only after a successful store, and candidates are recomputed each cycle (:91), so an inflating frame is retried every cycle. OOM-killing the single collector process (512m limit) causes a restart loop that stops aircraft and SIGMET collection too. The trigger requires the authenticated HTTPS KMA API to serve a malicious or corrupt highly compressible file, which is unlikely. Hence low.
fix_v: In read_echo: `d = zlib.decompressobj(16 + zlib.MAX_WBITS); raw = d.decompress(gz_bytes, MAX_RAW); if d.unconsumed_tail or not d.eof: raise ValueError('decompressed size exceeds cap')` with `MAX_RAW = 64 * 1024 * 1024`. After parse_header, also reject `not (0 < nx <= 4096 and 0 < ny <= 4096)`. Optionally run read_echo/render_mercator_png via `await asyncio.to_thread(...)` so the CPU-heavy decode does not block the other jobs' event loop.

title: The SIGMET 2,000-point cap truncates rings (silently storing a different hazard polygon); ring count and parse time are unbounded
evidence: sigmet_parse.py:26 `raw_rings = coords if item.get("geom") == "AREAS" else [coords]` has no cap on the number of rings. :37 `rings.append(pts[:MAX_POINTS])` keeps the first 2,000 vertices, then :72-73 closes the ring back to vertex 0 and :76-83 make_valid/unary_union run on it with no time budget. Design 6.1 asks for '폴리곤 점 ≤ 2,000, 면적 상한, 파싱 타임아웃'.
failure_scenario: A SIGMET with 2,500 vertices is stored, drawn and used for intersection as the polygon of its first 2,000 points plus a closing chord, with no excluded_reason. Aircraft inside the real area get no alert, and the map shows an area the issuer never published, which violates the data-honesty rule. An AREAS payload with thousands of 2,000-point rings (within the 20 MB cap) keeps unary_union busy for minutes and stalls the SIGMET job.
fix: If len(pts) > MAX_POINTS, return (None, "too_many_points") so it appears as 판정 제외 instead of truncating. Cap total vertices across rings (e.g. 5,000) and the ring count. Run build_geometry under a time budget (asyncio.wait_for around run_in_executor) and exclude on timeout.
reason: Code confirmed. sigmet_parse.py:37 `rings.append(pts[:MAX_POINTS])` silently truncates a ring longer than 2,000 vertices, and :72-73 then closes it back to vertex 0. That stores and draws a polygon the issuer never published, with no excluded_reason. This violates the project's data-honesty rule and the design's intent ('폴리곤 점 ≤ 2,000' as a cap, not truncation). :26 has no ring-count or total-vertex cap. The design's '파싱 타임아웃' is not implemented: parse_isigmet is called synchronously on the event loop (jobs/weather.py:90). Real-world reachability is very low. The last 40 AWC payloads peak at 61 points per ring and 2 rings, so this only triggers on anomalous upstream data.
fix_v: In _rings, return a flag instead of truncating. In build_geometry, `if any(len(r) > MAX_POINTS for r in raw_rings): return None, "too_many_points"`, and also exclude with `too_many_rings` when `len(raw_rings) > 50` or when the total vertex count exceeds 10,000. The hard caps are the real guard against slow unary_union. Optionally run the parse via `await asyncio.wait_for(asyncio.to_thread(...), 10)` to unblock the loop. A timed-out thread keeps running, so it is not a substitute for the caps.

title: Data honesty: an unpublished SIGMET base is shown as 'SFC', and a missing or invalid top is shown as '∞'

The schema requires integer base_ft, and the DB has `base_ft integer not null default 0`. web lib/format.ts:30 `${base === 0 ? "SFC" : fmtAlt(base)} – ${top == null ? "∞" : fmtAlt(top)}`, rendered at SigmetCard.tsx:24 as '고도대'. Live DB: 94 of 130 active SIGMETs have base_ft=0 while raw_text contains no SFC/SURFACE, e.g. `OEJD ... EMBD TS FCST WI ... TOP ABV FL380`, which the card shows as 'SFC – FL380'. 8 active SIGMETs have top null and show '∞'.

A reported top that is below the base (bad data) is replaced by '∞' (no upper limit) instead of being flagged. Both are inferred values displayed as data, contrary to the project rule 'unknown = —'. Treating the base as 0 in the engine is a defensible conservative assumption, but it is unlabelled in the UI and in the alert evidence (band_ft [0, top]).

Render '— (미기재)' or 'TOP FL380' from the actual fields, and show '—' for a missing top. For intersection, keep 0 as an explicit assumption and label it in evidence ('하한 미기재 → 지상부터로 간주'). When top < base, set a quality flag or excluded_reason instead of converting it to ∞.
reason: Confirmed with live data. sigmet_parse.py:116 maps a missing base to 0, :118-119 turns top<base into None, and :166 does the same for AIRMET/US SIGMET. web lib/format.ts:30 renders `base === 0 ? "SFC"` and `top == null ? "∞"`, shown as 고도대 in SigmetCard.tsx:24 and EvidenceCard.tsx:11 (band_ft from AlertStateMachine.java:128/146, with -1 meaning null). Live DB: of 122 currently valid SIGMETs, 100 have base_ft=0, 86 of them without SFC/SURFACE in raw_text, and 8 have top_ft null. The raw AWC payload for UTAA SIGMET 2 has `base=None top=None`, while its bulletin text says `TOP FL380`. Design §10.4 line 1220 prescribes 'base null → 0(SFC)'. The user's standing rule (unknown = '—', estimates must be labelled) overrides this for display. Keeping 0 as the engine's conservative assumption is fine if it is labelled.

Collector: `base_ft = int(base) if ... else None`. When top < base, keep both values and set a quality event instead of nulling top. Web band(): render null base as '— (미기재)' and null top as '— (미기재)', never 'SFC'/'∞' unless those values come from the source. title: Hysteresis counts engine cycles, not observations: global aircraft get ENTERED/LEFT from one position report; evidence falsely says 'confirmations: 2'
evidence: AlertStateMachine.java:49-55 `t.inside++; t.outside = 0; if (!t.confirmed && t.inside >= ENTER_CONFIRM)` and :68-72 `t.outside++; ... if (t.outside >= LEAVE_CONFIRM)` increment once per step() call. EngineService.java:57-68 calls run() on every SigmetsUpdated and on every SnapshotUpdated of either scope; :80-81 `new HashMap<>(snapshots.global().states()); all.putAll(snapshots.region().states())` re-feeds the same global positions (updated only every 120 s) to every 10 s region cycle. AlertStateMachine.java:134 `ev.put("confirmations", ENTER_CONFIRM)` is a constant; EvidenceCard.tsx:21 `${String(ev.confirmations ?? 2)}회` also defaults to 2. DB check (read-only, last 3 h): for OBSERVED alerts from opensky, 1,531 of 3,341 had the aircraft's previous recorded position (track_point, within 10 min before evidence.seen_at) OUTSIDE the SIGMET volume, i.e. ENTERED was confirmed by a single inside report; region providers 4/178 (the extra global/SIGMET re-runs). Re-entry within 5 min after LEFT: opensky 333/2,473.
failure_scenario: OpenSky reports aircraft X once inside a TS SIGMET (a single noisy or boundary position). The next region cycle 10 s later re-evaluates the same frozen global position, t.inside reaches 2 and ENTERED is emitted, persisted and broadcast with evidence 'confirmations: 2' / UI '연속 확인 2회'. Two minutes later the next global fetch puts X outside; 3 region cycles (30 s) later LEFT fires from that single outside report. The flicker suppression FR-09 promises does not exist for ~98% of tracked aircraft, and the evidence card states a fact (two consecutive confirmations) that never happened.
fix: Count only distinct observations: store lastSeenAt per Track key and increment inside/outside only when the aircraft's seenAt advanced since the previous count (absence should be counted by elapsed time, see COR-4). Do not let SigmetsUpdated/global-only re-runs advance region aircraft counters. Record the actual seen_at timestamps of the confirming observations in evidence (e.g. confirmations: [t1,t2]) and remove the `?? 2` default in EvidenceCard (render '—' when absent).
reason: Confirmed in the code. AlertStateMachine.java:52-54 (`t.inside++; t.outside = 0; if (!t.confirmed && t.inside >= ENTER_CONFIRM)`) and :69-72 count one step per step() call, not per new observation. EngineService.java:57-68 calls run() on every SigmetsUpdated and on every SnapshotUpdated. :80-81 feed the unchanged global states (120 s poll) into every 10 s region cycle, so a single OpenSky report inside a SIGMET is 'confirmed' on the next region cycle. :134 `ev.put("confirmations", ENTER_CONFIRM)` is a constant, and EvidenceCard.tsx:21 `${String(ev.confirmations ?? 2)}회` defaults to 2 as well. DB probe (last 3 h, method=observed_point_in_polygon): opensky had 1,389 of 3,560 ENTERED alerts whose previous track_point (within 10 min before evidence.seen_at) lay horizontally OUTSIDE the SIGMET polygon; adsb_fi 3/69, adsb_lol 0/83. So ENTERED is routinely confirmed from one report while the evidence claims two.

Increment inside/outside only when states.get(hex).seenAt() is after lastCountedSeenAt, so re-runs from SigmetsUpdated or region cycles over unchanged global data do not count. Handle absence separately (see COR-4). Record the real observation timestamps in evidence (e.g. `confirmations_seen_at: [t1, t2]`) instead of the constant ENTER_CONFIRM. In EvidenceCard.tsx:21, drop `?? 2` and render '—' when the field is absent.

title: Alert IDs from epoch-seconds counter collide after every restart: inserts fail and UPDATE-by-id corrupts unrelated historical alerts
evidence: EngineService.java:41 `new AtomicLong(System.currentTimeMillis() / 1000)`; AlertRepository.java:51-54 `INSERT INTO alert_event (id, ...) ... ON CONFLICT (hex, sigmet_id, kind, entered_at) DO NOTHING` (arbiter is not the PK); :58 `UPDATE alert_event SET eta_s = :eta, evidence = :ev::jsonb WHERE id = :id`; :60 `UPDATE alert_event SET left_at = :left WHERE id = :id AND left_at IS NULL`. V1__init.sql:70 `id bigserial PRIMARY KEY` sequence is never used. Live data: id - epoch(entered_at) drift reached +390 (alerts generated faster than 1/s). api log since the 11:19:24 restart: 131 `DuplicateKeyException ... alert_event_pkey` ('alert persist failed (PREDICTED|ENTERED)'). DB: 182 rows with kind='OBSERVED' now carry `evidence.method='dead_reckoning_10min'` and non-null eta_s (e.g. id 1790503088, hex 151e19, OBSERVED, eta_s 190).
failure_scenario: The api has issued ids up to now+390. It restarts (40 s). The new counter starts at now+40, so the next ~350 ENTERED/PREDICTED inserts hit existing PKs and are lost from history. Subsequent PREDICTION_UPDATED/LEFT/PREDICTION_CLEARED events for those new alerts run `WHERE id = :id` against the OLD rows: an old OBSERVED alert gets prediction evidence/ETA written into it, and orphaned old alerts get a left_at belonging to a different aircraft. History, replay evidence and dwell statistics are silently corrupted.
fix: Let the DB assign ids (INSERT ... RETURNING id via nextval('alert_event_id_seq')) or seed the in-memory counter at startup from `SELECT max(id) FROM alert_event` (or use a UUID/ULID). Include the natural key (hex, sigmet_id, kind, entered_at) in the UPDATE WHERE clauses as a guard. Repair the 182 corrupted rows (kind='OBSERVED' AND evidence->>'method'='dead_reckoning_10min').
reason: Confirmed. EngineService.java:41 `new AtomicLong(System.currentTimeMillis() / 1000)` seeds ids from wall-clock seconds. With about 9k aircraft, alerts are issued faster than 1/s, so the counter runs ahead of the clock. The max observed id minus epoch(entered_at) is +390. At the 11:19:24 restart the new counter started at about 1790507964, while the previous run had already issued ids up to 1790508093. The api log shows 131 `alert persist failed (ENTERED|PREDICTED): DuplicateKeyException`: the INSERT at AlertRepository.java:51-54 only arbitrates on the natural key, so a PK conflict throws. The UPDATEs at :58 and :60 match by `WHERE id = :id` alone, so they then hit the OLD rows. DB: 182 rows with kind='OBSERVED' now carry evidence.method='dead_reckoning_10min' and a non-null eta_s (e.g. id 1790508075, hex 4bb2ab, entered 11:17:32, judged_at 11:23:32). The bigserial sequence (V1__init.sql:70) is never used.
fix_v: Stop deriving ids from the clock. Add a V3 migration `SELECT setval('alert_event_id_seq', GREATEST((SELECT coalesce(max(id),1) FROM alert_event), 1))` and have the FSM's LongSupplier take ids from the sequence (block-allocate, e.g. `SELECT nextval('alert_event_id_seq') FROM generate_series(1,100)`). The quick alternative is to seed the AtomicLong at startup from `SELECT max(id) FROM alert_event`. Guard both UPDATEs with the natural key: `WHERE id = :id AND hex = :hex AND sigmet_id = :sig AND kind = :kind`. Repair `kind='OBSERVED' AND evidence->>'method'='dead_reckoning_10min'` (182 rows), and treat left_at on ids in the collision range 1790507964-1790508093 as suspect.

title: Stale/frozen global positions are treated as current by the engine and the map (no position-age cutoff; global snapshot never expires)
evidence: EngineService.java:80 `new HashMap<>(snapshots.global().states())` — no seen_at or snapshot-age filter; quality.py:55-70 has speed/alt/future/jump rules but no max-age rule; normalize.py:124 `seen_at = datetime.fromtimestamp(tpos, UTC)` keeps OpenSky time_position however old. aircraft.py:105-106 on low credits sets `_global_paused_until = midnight + 1 day` and publishes nothing, so SnapshotStore keeps the last global snapshot indefinitely. StatusBar.tsx:13 only shows `status.region.lag_s`; global staleness (StatusService.java:49 `g.stale(now, 300)`) is never surfaced. Live: alert 1790508662 (hex 4bd18a) ENTERED at 11:27:39 with evidence seen_at 11:13:36 (14 min old); track_point shows OpenSky kept returning the 11:13:36 position on every fetch until 11:41:49. In the last 10 min 1,651 of 41,783 OpenSky positions were >60 s old at fetch (max 146 s).
failure_scenario: An aircraft leaves OpenSky coverage; OpenSky keeps listing it with a frozen time_position. The engine judges the 14-minute-old point to be 'inside' and issues an OBSERVED ENTERED alert, and it keeps predicting from that point. If OpenSky credits run low at 09:00 UTC, the ~8,000 aircraft from the last global fetch stay frozen on the world map and in the FSM until 00:00 UTC: observed alerts stay INSIDE and predictions keep running on positions up to 15 h old, with no stale badge in the UI.
fix: Drop states older than a threshold (e.g. seen_at older than 60 s region / 180 s global) in the collector gate (a 'stale_position' quarantine rule) and again in the engine (skip hits/predictions when now - seenAt > threshold). Expire the global snapshot in the api when fetchedAt is older than 2x global_poll_s: treat it as empty for the engine and mark it STALE for the map. Show global lag/STALE in StatusBar when the world layer is visible.
reason: Confirmed. Neither the engine (EngineService.java:80-86, IntersectionEngine.observe/predict) nor the collector gate (quality.py:55-70: speed, alt, future, jump only) has any position-age cutoff. normalize.py:124 keeps OpenSky time_position however old. aircraft.py:105-106 pauses global until the next UTC midnight and publishes nothing, and SnapshotStore keeps the last global snapshot indefinitely. The staleness flag (StatusService.java:49 `g.stale(now, 300)`) is never used by the engine, and StatusBar.tsx:13 shows only region lag. Live: alert 1790508662 (hex 4bd18a, opensky) was ENTERED at 11:27:39 with evidence seen_at 11:13:36, i.e. a 14-minute-old position judged as 'observed inside'. Last 10 min: 1,746 of 42,337 OpenSky points were more than 60 s old at fetch (max 5m21s).
fix_v: (1) Collector: add a gate rule `stale_position` (e.g. now - seen_at > 60 s for region, > 180 s for global) that quarantines the state. (2) Engine: skip observe/predict for states with Duration.between(seenAt, now) above the same threshold. Treat the global snapshot as empty in EngineService.run when `snapshots.global().stale(now, 2 * globalPollS)`. (3) Web: show a global lag/STALE badge in StatusBar when global data is on the map.

title: Aircraft that drop out of the feed while inside a SIGMET are reported as LEFT (이탈), with a fabricated left_at
evidence: AlertStateMachine.java:63 comment `// 이탈 확인 (스냅샷에서 사라진 기체도 '밖' 으로 센다)`; :64-76 any key not in insideNow increments outside, and after 3 cycles `Alert left = withLeft(t.alert, now); out.add(new Event(EventType.LEFT, left));`. No distinction between 'observed outside' and 'no data'. DB (last 3 h): for closed OBSERVED alerts, the last recorded position before left_at was still inside the SIGMET volume (valid, in band) for adsb_lol 58/72, adsb_fi 46/60, opensky 1,008/2,593; in 45/36/895 of those the aircraft had no new position for over 40 s before LEFT (mean gap 97 s region, 352 s opensky). MaintenanceJobs.java:97 computes alert_dwell_avg_s from these left_at values.
failure_scenario: A region aircraft descends below receiver coverage while inside a TURB SIGMET, so readsb stops giving it lat/lon. Three 10 s cycles later the system emits LEFT with left_at = now, the panel shows it exited, history and replay show a clean exit time, and dwell statistics use that invented exit time. When the aircraft reappears inside, a new ENTERED is created (flapping).
fix: Count 'absent' separately from 'observed outside': require LEAVE_CONFIRM distinct outside observations for LEFT. On absence beyond a timeout, emit a distinct event (e.g. LOST / SIGNAL_LOST) with left_at = NULL, or store `end_reason='lost'` with last_seen_at = the last seen_at inside. Exclude lost alerts from dwell averages.
reason: Confirmed. AlertStateMachine.java:63-76: any confirmed key not in insideNow gets `t.outside++`, including aircraft missing from the snapshot (the comment says so), and after 3 steps it emits LEFT with `withLeft(t.alert, now)`. DB probe restricted to alerts entered after 11:40 (clean of the COR-2 id collisions): for closed OBSERVED alerts, the last track_point before left_at was still inside the polygon and band (and before valid_to) in adsb_fi 2/4, adsb_lol 3/5 and opensky 91/348, almost all with no newer position for more than 40 s. So LEFT/left_at reports an exit that was never observed.
fix_v: Count only observed-outside states toward LEAVE_CONFIRM. When a key's aircraft is absent from `all`, do not increment outside. Instead, once now - lastSeenAt exceeds a timeout (e.g. 60 s region, 300 s global), close the alert with a distinct end reason: evidence.end_reason='signal_lost', left_at = last seen_at inside (or NULL plus a last_seen_at column). The UI should show '신호 소실' rather than '이탈'. Exclude signal_lost rows from the alert_dwell_avg_s query.

title: SIGMET with unknown top (AWC top=null) is treated and displayed as unbounded ('∞'), even when the raw text states TOP FLxxx
evidence: sigmet_parse.py:115-119 `top_ft = int(top) if isinstance(top, int | float) else None` and `if top_ft is not None and top_ft < base_ft: top_ft = None`; SigmetRecord.java:16 `(topFt == null || altFt <= topFt)`; format.ts:30 `top == null ? "∞"`; AlertStateMachine.java:128 `s.topFt() == null ? -1` → EvidenceCard.tsx:11 renders ∞. Live: AWC raw item ZYSH:4 has `top: None` while rawSigmet says 'EMBD TS FCST ... TOP FL300'; UTAA:2 `top: None`, raw 'TOP FL380'. 8 of 123 active SIGMETs have top_ft null.
failure_scenario: An aircraft cruising at FL390 over the ZYSH TS area (real top FL300) is judged INSIDE: an OBSERVED alert is issued and the evidence card shows band 'SFC – ∞', a value no source gave. Where AWC's decoder has top<base, the code also silently widens the band to infinity. This conflicts with the project rule that unknown values are shown as '—'.
fix: Keep top_ft null as 'unknown', not 'unlimited': render '—' / '상한 미상' in the UI and evidence. Record `top_source`. Where the top can be read deterministically from the official raw text (regex `TOP (ABV )?FL(\d{3})`), store it with source='raw_text'. In the engine, either skip the vertical test with a labelled 'band unknown' flag in evidence, or do not raise OBSERVED alerts when the band is unknown. For top<base, set excluded_reason='invalid_band' instead of widening it.
reason: Confirmed. sigmet_parse.py:117-119 maps AWC top=null, and also top<base, to None. SigmetRecord.java:16 treats null as unbounded, AlertStateMachine.java:128 emits -1, and format.ts:30 renders '∞'. Design 10.4 item 3 says 'top null → 상한 없음', but the live raw texts contradict that: 8 active SIGMETs have top_ft NULL, and 5 of them state a top in the official text (ZYSH:4 'TOP FL300', UTAA:2 'TOP FL380', FCCC:B2/C1 'TOP FL420'). An aircraft at FL390 in ZYSH:4 is therefore judged INSIDE and shown 'SFC – ∞', which breaks the unknown='—' rule.
fix_v: In parse_isigmet, when `top` is null, parse the raw text deterministically with the regex `\bTOP (?:ABV )?FL(\d{3})\b` and set top_ft with top_source='raw_text'; otherwise leave top_ft null with top_source='unknown'. Replace the top<base widening with excluded_reason='invalid_band'. In the UI, render an unknown top as '—' / '상한 미상' instead of '∞' (format.ts:30, EvidenceCard.tsx:11). In the engine, add evidence.band_top_known=false when topFt is null, so an OBSERVED alert above a raw-text-less TS SIGMET is marked as based on an unknown top.

title: WS diff version gaps are created by the server itself (empty diffs not sent; global-scope versions skipped for region sessions), so the client drops real diffs and forces full resyncs
evidence: WsHub.java (HEAD):97 `if (global && !s.world) continue;` and (HEAD):141 / (working tree):157 `if (diff == null || diff.isEmpty()) { s.lastSentVersion = version; return; }` (no message is sent, but the shared version counter from SnapshotStore.nextVersion() still advances). ws-protocol.ts:10 `return incomingV > lastV + 1 || incomingV <= lastV;`; ws.ts:92 `if (needsResync(this.lastV, v)) { this.resync(); return; }` discards the diff. Live probe (bbox 126.3,37.3,126.9,37.6, zoom 10): `snapshot v=179` → `diff v=181 ... GAP` (v=180 was the global snapshot not sent to region sessions).
failure_scenario: A viewport over an airport where the only aircraft are parked produces empty diffs for several cycles (no message sent). When a departing aircraft then moves, the diff arrives with v = lastV+3, the client discards it and requests resync, and the update only appears one cycle later through a full snapshot. Every such event costs a dropped update plus a full-snapshot transfer. On HEAD this also happens after every 120 s global event for non-world sessions. The in-progress change that sends global events to every session removes only the second cause.
fix: Make continuity explicit: include `base_v` (the session's lastSentVersion) in every diff and have the client check base_v === lastV instead of v === lastV+1. Alternatively always send a (tiny) diff even when empty, and use a per-session sequence number instead of the global snapshot version.
reason: Confirmed, but the impact is smaller than stated. HEAD (the running image: the status snapshot reports scope 'region' even though global has 9,263 aircraft) skips global versions for non-world sessions (`if (global && !s.world) continue;`). Both HEAD :141 and the working tree WsHub.java:157 advance lastSentVersion on an empty diff without sending anything, and ws-protocol.ts:10 plus ws.ts:92 treat any jump as a gap and discard the diff. My probe over 126.3,37.3,126.9,37.6 went v262 → (v263 global, skipped) → snapshot v264. It was masked there by the 30 s resync, but a diff would have been dropped. The consequence is one discarded diff plus a full snapshot on the next cycle (≤10 s delay). State self-heals and the periodic 30 s full resync already bounds it, so this is not a correctness hazard: low.
fix_v: Add `base_v` to DiffMsg: the session's lastSentVersion before this diff, i.e. the version of the last message actually delivered. On the client, resync only when base_v !== lastV. Also, stop assigning `s.lastSentVersion = version` on the empty-diff path in WsHub.fanoutOne (then base_v stays correct without sending empty messages).

title: Alerts/SIGMET/radar state is never resynced after pause/resume or a backpressure drop, so the alert panel silently diverges
evidence: WsHub.java (HEAD):106 `if (s.subscribed()) pool.submit(() -> sendSigmets(...))` and :119 `if (s.subscribed()) pool.submit(() -> s.sendOrDrop(payload))` skip paused sessions (WsSession.java:49 `hello && bbox != null && !paused`). SkyWsHandler.java:78 `case "resume" -> { s.paused = false; s.needsResync = true; }`; needsResync only triggers WsHub.sendFull (aircraft). WsSession.java:52-60 sendOrDrop drops any message (including alerts_batch) when the buffer is over half full and sets needsResync, which again only re-sends aircraft. The full 'alerts' list is sent only from sendInitial on subscribe.
failure_scenario: A user switches browser tabs for 10 min (MapView sends pause). During that time 40 ENTERED/LEFT/PREDICTED events are skipped. On return, resume re-sends aircraft only: the panel still lists alerts that have ended and lacks new ones, and SIGMET polygons are up to 5 min stale, until the user pans the map. A single backpressure drop of an alerts_batch has the same effect.
fix: On resume and on needsResync, run the same path as sendInitial (full snapshot + sigmets + radar + alerts list), or add alert/sigmet version numbers to the messages and let the client request what it is missing. Consider sending the alert list with the periodic 30 s resync.
reason: Confirmed. WsSession.java:50 subscribed() excludes paused sessions, so while paused, WsHub.onAlerts/onSigmets/onRadar (working tree :122, :127, :135) skip them. MapView.tsx:120 sends pause on every tab hide. SkyWsHandler.java:78 resume only sets needsResync, which only triggers sendFull (aircraft, WsHub.java:173-189). sendOrDrop (WsSession.java:53-62) can drop an alerts_batch and again only needsResync is set. The full 'alerts' list is sent only in sendInitial (on subscribe), and the web code never refetches /api/v1/alerts (no usage found). After a long tab switch, the alert panel keeps ended alerts and misses new ones until the user pans.
fix_v: In SkyWsHandler, change resume to `{ s.paused = false; s.needsResync = true; hub.sendInitial(s, engine.activeAlerts(null)); }` (sigmets + radar + alerts + snapshot). In sendOrDrop, set a separate `needsStateResync` flag when a non-diff message is dropped, and have fanoutOne call the sendInitial path when it is set. Optionally attach the alerts list to the 30 s full resync.

title: World-view encoding strips seen_at/gs/on_ground/squawk, so the client shows every world aircraft as fresh (age 0, never stale/removed) and hides emergencies
evidence: WsMessages.java:33-39 world branch puts only hex, lat, lon, alt_ft, track_deg, callsign. interpolate.worker.js:16 `var seenMs = s.seen_at ? Date.parse(s.seen_at) : nowMs;` (interpolate.ts:30 same) → dt = 0 → `stale: false`, `age_s: 0`, never exceeds REMOVE_AFTER_S; emergency derives from the missing squawk. Live probe (bbox 60,0,170,60, zoom 3): snapshot keys `['alt_ft','callsign','hex','lat','lon','track_deg']`. ws.ts:99 also forces `stale: false` on every diff regardless of region lag.
failure_scenario: At zoom ≤ 5, OpenSky positions that are 2–15 min old (or frozen for hours, COR-3) are drawn at full opacity as live aircraft. This contradicts the /about page promise ('60 s 이상 미수신은 반투명, 300 s 초과는 제거'). A 7700 squawk is not highlighted in world view. The same aircraft is hidden (age > 300 s) at zoom 6 but visible and 'fresh' at zoom 5.
fix: Keep seen_at in the world encoding (compactly, e.g. `age_s` as an integer or epoch seconds) plus squawk/emergency. In the worker, treat a missing seen_at as unknown age (stale=true or excluded), never as age 0. Derive the diff `stale` flag from server data instead of hard-coding false.
reason: Confirmed. The world branch in WsMessages.java:33-39 emits only hex, lat, lon, alt_ft, track_deg and callsign (no seen_at, gs_kt, on_ground, squawk). interpolate.worker.js:16 / interpolate.ts:30 `var seenMs = s.seen_at ? Date.parse(s.seen_at) : nowMs;` then gives age 0, stale=false, and the REMOVE_AFTER_S cut never applies. Emergency is derived from s.squawk (worker :20), so it is always false in world view. ws.ts:99 hard-codes `stale: false` on every diff. At zoom ≤5, frozen or old OpenSky positions (COR-3) are therefore drawn as fresh, contrary to the 60 s/300 s rule.
fix_v: Add `seen_at` (or an integer `age_s`) and `squawk` (or an `emergency` boolean) to the world encoding in WsMessages.encode. In predict() (worker and interpolate.ts), treat a missing seen_at as unknown age: stale=true and age_s=null, not 0. In ws.ts:99, stop forcing stale:false; keep the value from the last snapshot or status.

title: Prediction ETA and entry-time validity are computed from the position timestamp, not from now; ETA is also frozen between updates
evidence: IntersectionEngine.java:61-64 `path[0] = new Coordinate(a.lon(), a.lat()); ... DeadReckoning.predict(..., i * PREDICT_STEP_S)` starts dead reckoning at seen_at's position, but :77 `Instant entryTime = now.plusSeconds((long) tEntry);` and eta_s is reported relative to the judgement time. The predicted evidence (AlertStateMachine.java:145-154) has no seen_at, only `judged_at`. :90 updates only when `Math.abs(prev.etaS() - p.etaS()) >= 30`. Observed position age at judgement averages 40 s (max 843 s) for opensky alerts.
failure_scenario: A global aircraft's position is 110 s old when judged. The engine reports 'ETA 5m 00s' from judged_at, but the aircraft is already about 110 s further along, so the true ETA is about 3m 10s. The global position is frozen for 120 s, so the same ETA is re-derived each cycle and never counts down, then jumps by about 2 min. validAt(entryTime) can also accept or reject the wrong SIGMET near its valid_from/valid_to.
fix: Dead-reckon from seen_at to now first, or compute tEntry from path[0] and then subtract age = now - seenAt (drop the prediction if tEntry - age < 0). Store seen_at/position_age_s in predicted evidence. Have the client count ETA down from judged_at (ETA_remaining = eta_s - (now - judged_at)) or re-emit updates when the displayed ETA drifts.
reason: Confirmed. IntersectionEngine.java:61-64 dead-reckons from the position as of seen_at, so tEntry is measured from seen_at. But :77 `Instant entryTime = now.plusSeconds((long) tEntry)` and eta_s = tEntry are presented relative to judged_at. For global aircraft, whose positions are up to 120 s plus time_position age old, the ETA is overstated by that age, and validAt(entryTime) is evaluated at the wrong instant. AlertStateMachine.java:90 only re-emits when |ΔETA| ≥ 30 s, and AlertPanel.tsx:56 renders the static `fmtEta(a.eta_s)` with no countdown, so the displayed ETA is frozen between updates. Predicted evidence (:145-154) carries no seen_at.
fix_v: In predictOne compute `age = max(0, now - a.seenAt())`, set `eta = tEntry - age`, and drop the prediction if eta < 0; use `entryTime = a.seenAt().plusSeconds(tEntry)` for validAt. Add `seen_at` and `position_age_s` to predicted evidence. In the client, display `max(0, eta_s - (Date.now() - judged_at)/1000)`, ticking each second.

title: Orphaned alerts: every api restart leaves active alerts open forever (left_at NULL) in history
evidence: FSM state is only in memory (AlertStateMachine.java:37-38 `observed`/`predicted` HashMaps). Nothing closes open rows at startup or shutdown. AlertRepository.java:65-80 history returns them with left_at null. Live: 2,008 OBSERVED rows with left_at IS NULL (940 older than 1 h), while /api/v1/alerts?kind=observed reports 269 active in memory. PREDICTED: 453 open rows.
failure_scenario: The api restarts while 300 alerts are active. The new FSM re-detects the aircraft and inserts new ENTERED rows, but the 300 old rows never get left_at. /api/v1/alerts/history and replay show those aircraft as still inside SIGMETs from hours or days ago, and such alerts are excluded from dwell statistics, which skews them.
fix: On startup (before the first engine cycle) close dangling rows: `UPDATE alert_event SET left_at = <last known engine time>, evidence = evidence || '{"end_reason":"api_restart"}' WHERE left_at IS NULL`. Alternatively persist FSM state or re-hydrate it from open rows. Also close open rows in a SmartLifecycle.stop().
reason: Confirmed. FSM state is memory-only (AlertStateMachine.java:37-38), and nothing closes open rows on startup or shutdown (the only left_at write is AlertRepository.java:60). DB: 1,739 OBSERVED and 390 PREDICTED rows entered before the 11:19 restart still have left_at NULL. Since 11:22, the set of open rows (360) exactly equals the in-memory active set (360), so the orphans come from restarts (plus COR-2 collisions), not steady-state operation. /alerts/history returns them as still inside.
fix_v: In a startup hook that runs before StreamConsumer starts (e.g. an ApplicationRunner, or a SmartLifecycle with a lower phase), run `UPDATE alert_event SET left_at = coalesce((evidence->>'judged_at')::timestamptz, entered_at), evidence = evidence || '{"end_reason":"api_restart"}' WHERE left_at IS NULL`. Mirror this in a stop() hook, using now(). Exclude end_reason='api_restart' rows from dwell statistics.

title: Vertical entry into a SIGMET band is never predicted (start point horizontally inside → no prediction)
evidence: IntersectionEngine.java:86-88 `Point start = ...; if (it.prepared().intersects(start)) return -1;` and :73-78 `if (tEntry < 0) continue; ... if (!it.sigmet().bandContains(altAtEntry) ...) continue;` — altitude is checked only at the first horizontal crossing, so the band is never tested along the rest of the path. Not documented as a limitation in ADR-010 or on /about.
failure_scenario: An aircraft climbs at 2,000 fpm through FL200 horizontally inside 'ZLHW SEV TURB ABV FL230'. It will enter the band in about 90 s, but firstIntersectionSeconds returns -1 because the start point is inside the polygon, so no PREDICTED alert is raised. Likewise, an aircraft that crosses the polygon edge below the base and then climbs into the band is missed.
fix: Test the 3D condition along the path: for each 60 s step (with sub-step interpolation) evaluate horizontalInside(t) && bandContains(alt(t)) && validAt(now+t), and report the first t where it becomes true (including when the start is horizontally inside but outside the band). Add a unit test for the climb-into-band case.
reason: The behaviour is confirmed. IntersectionEngine.java:87-88 returns -1 when the start point is horizontally inside, and :76-78 check the band only at the first horizontal crossing. A climb or descent into the band, whether starting inside or after crossing the edge outside the band, is never PREDICTED. However, this follows the design's own pseudo-code (10.3: alt_at_entry evaluated only at t_entry) and ADR-010 ('폴리곤과 만나는 첫 시각 ... 그때의 고도'). The OBSERVED alert still fires on actual entry. It is a missing-coverage limitation rather than a wrong result, so the severity is low, not medium.
fix_v: In predictOne, sample t = 0..600 s (e.g. every 10 s) and take the first t with prepared.intersects(point(t)) && bandContains(alt0 + vr*t/60) && validAt(seenAt + t), skipping only the case where that condition already holds at t=0 (the observed domain). Add a unit test for 'horizontally inside, climbing into ABV FL230'. At minimum, document the limitation on /about and in ADR-010.

title: Region center/radius diverge between api (env) and collector (Redis runtime settings seeded from DB); .env REGION_CENTER is silently ignored by the collector
evidence: api uses env only: StatusService.java:47 `"center", List.of(props.regionLat(), props.regionLon()), "radius_nm", props.regionRadiusNm()` and MaintenanceJobs.java:58-68 summary bbox from props. Collector: runtime_settings.py:61-68 reads `region_center`/`region_radius_nm` from the Redis hash, which StartupMirror/SettingsService.java:54-61 always fill from app_setting (seed V1__init.sql:145 `('region_center', '"36.5,127.8"')`). AlertPanel.tsx:19 filters by `status?.region.center`. SettingsService.java:77 regex `^-?\d{1,2}(\.\d+)?,-?\d{1,3}(\.\d+)?$` also accepts lat 99 / lon 999.
failure_scenario: An operator changes region_center to '35.5,139.7' (Tokyo) in /ops. The collector now polls around Tokyo, but /status still reports the Korea center, the AlertPanel 'Region' filter hides every Tokyo alert, and the hourly 1-minute summary averages the old Korea box (now fed only by 2-min global samples). Conversely, setting REGION_CENTER in .env changes the api but not the collector, because the startup mirror overwrites Redis with the DB seed. A value like '95,200' passes validation and yields an invalid provider bbox.
fix: Use a single source of truth: have the api read the region from app_setting (cached, refreshed on update) for status, summaries and the ws/REST filters, and seed app_setting from env on first boot. Validate ranges numerically (lat ∈ [-85,85], lon ∈ [-180,180]).
reason: Confirmed. The api's region comes only from env/props (StatusService.java:47, MaintenanceJobs.java:58-68). The collector's region comes from the Redis hash (runtime_settings.py:61-68, cache-first in _get), and SettingsService.mirror (:54-61) always fills that hash from app_setting, whose seed is V1__init.sql:145 '"36.5,127.8"'. Consequences: (a) an ops change to region_center moves the collector but not /status, AlertPanel's 'Region' filter (AlertPanel.tsx:19-25) or the 1-minute summary bbox; (b) REGION_CENTER in .env (compose.yml:88/:133) reaches the api but is overridden in the collector by the DB seed at startup. The validation regex at SettingsService.java:77 accepts lat 99 / lon 999.
fix_v: Make app_setting the single source. On first boot (e.g. in StartupMirror, via INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING semantics, or by a version=1 check), seed region_center/region_radius_nm from env. Have StatusService and MaintenanceJobs read the region through a cached SettingsService getter that is refreshed in update(). Replace the regex with numeric parsing that enforces lat ∈ [-85, 85] and lon ∈ [-180, 180].

title: KMA radar job re-downloads 3 already-discarded old frames every cycle (candidate list includes frames older than the kept window)
evidence: kma_radar.py:88-91 `have = {f["tm"] for f in await self._frames()}` (only the last 12 kept frames); `candidates = [tm for tm in listing.data if tm <= now_tm and tm not in have][-MAX_PER_CYCLE:]` also matches every earlier frame of the day. :158 `frames = sorted(...)[-KEEP_FRAMES:]` then immediately discards them. Collector log: the 11:12 cycle fetched tm=…1850, …1855, …1900 and the new …2005; 11:17 fetched …1855, …1900, …1905 and …2010; 11:42 fetched …1920, …1925, …1930 and …2035 — the same old frames are downloaded again and again.
failure_scenario: In steady state each 5-minute cycle makes 1 list call and 4 binary downloads (about 8 MB gz each, plus decode and reprojection of 2305×2881 grids) instead of 1. That is 4x the KMA API Hub call budget and CPU. Each run also writes 3 orphan `skywx:radar_kr:frame:{tm}` PNG keys to Redis that live for 3 h.
fix: Only consider frames newer than the oldest kept frame (e.g. `tm > min(have)` once 12 frames are kept), or newer than `now_tm - KEEP_FRAMES*5min`. Keep the backfill limited to the window that will actually be retained.
reason: Confirmed. kma_radar.py:88-91 takes `have` from the 12 kept frames only, so `tm not in have` also matches every earlier frame of the day, and `[-MAX_PER_CYCLE:]` picks 3 frames just older than the window plus the new one. :158 `[-KEEP_FRAMES:]` then discards the 3 old frames immediately. Collector log: every cycle since 11:37 downloads 4 frames (e.g. 12:03 → 1940, 1945, 1950, 2055), and 3 of them are re-downloads. ingest_run for hour 11: 12 runs, 48 frames. Each run also writes 3 orphan `skywx:radar_kr:frame:{tm}` keys with a 3 h TTL. Related: main.py:66-73 `limits` has no 'kma_radar' entry, so Budget.reserve uses limit 0, which the Lua script treats as unlimited. The configured budget_kma_radar=1000 is never enforced and nothing caps this 4x usage.
fix_v: In run_once, restrict candidates to frames newer than the retained window: `floor = min(have) if len(have) >= KEEP_FRAMES else ''` and `candidates = [tm for tm in listing.data if floor < tm <= now_tm and tm not in have][-MAX_PER_CYCLE:]`. Add `"kma_radar": settings.budget_kma_radar` to the limits dict in main.py.

title: SIGMETs withdrawn or superseded before valid_to keep their original validity in the DB, so replay and stats show them as still in force
evidence: SigmetRepository.java:40-47 only upserts records present in the current feed (`ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE SET valid_to = EXCLUDED.valid_to ...`), and nothing marks ids that disappear from a successful full fetch. :55-59 `validAt`: `WHERE valid_from <= :t AND valid_to > :t`. Live DB: 15 of 258 SIGMETs vanished from the AWC feed at least 15 min before their valid_to, and 7 are still 'valid' now (e.g. FAJO:F01 last fetched 10:09, valid_to 14:00; KZWY:JULIETT 4 last fetched 11:11, valid_to 12:30).
failure_scenario: KZWY re-issues a SIGMET as a new series at 11:12 (the old one is cancelled). Replay at 12:00 draws both the withdrawn and the new polygon as valid hazards, and stats count the withdrawn SIGMET for extra days, although AWC no longer published it.
fix: When a successful complete fetch no longer contains an id that is still within its valid time, set `withdrawn_at = fetched_at` (new column) and use `COALESCE(withdrawn_at, valid_to)` as the effective end in validAt, stats and replay. Do this only for fetches where both feeds succeeded (see COR-17).
reason: Confirmed. SigmetRepository.java:27-53 only upserts records present in the current feed, and :55-59 validAt uses the original valid_to. DB now: 7 SIGMETs whose last fetched_at is more than 15 min older than the latest fetch are still within valid_to (e.g. RJJJ:E03 last fetched 10:09, valid_to 13:09; KZWY:JULIETT 4 last fetched 11:11, valid_to 12:30). The live map and engine are unaffected: SigmetStore.replace swaps in the whole set. Only replay (HistoryController.java:53) draws withdrawn polygons as valid, and stats count an issued SIGMET, which is arguably still correct. That makes the severity low, not medium.
fix_v: Add a column `withdrawn_at timestamptz`. After a fetch in which both AWC feeds succeeded (needs a flag from the collector, see COR-17), run `UPDATE sigmet SET withdrawn_at = :fetched WHERE provider IN (...) AND valid_to > :fetched AND withdrawn_at IS NULL AND id <> ALL(:ids)`. Use `coalesce(withdrawn_at, valid_to) > :t` in validAt.

title: Alert persistence runs each batch on a new virtual thread: later UPDATEs (LEFT/CLEARED/UPDATED) can execute before the INSERT they refer to
evidence: AlertRepository.java:36-41 `Thread.ofVirtual().start(() -> { for (...) persist(ev); })` for each AlertsChanged. ENTERED/PREDICTED do a SIGMET upsert plus an INSERT (:49-56), while LEFT/CLEARED are one `UPDATE ... WHERE id = :id AND left_at IS NULL` (:60). EngineService runs back to back on SigmetsUpdated (:57-63) and on consecutive stream messages in the same XREADGROUP batch (count 10), producing batches milliseconds apart; a batch with 86 events was observed live.
failure_scenario: The SIGMET update re-run emits PREDICTED id=X (thread A: SIGMET upsert + insert, slower). Milliseconds later the next snapshot run emits PREDICTION_CLEARED id=X (thread B). B's UPDATE runs first and matches 0 rows, then A inserts, so the row stays open (left_at NULL) forever. PREDICTION_UPDATED can be lost the same way.

ENTERED/PREDICTED do a SIGMET upsert plus an INSERT (:49-56), while a later batch's UPDATE (:58/:60) can run first and match 0 rows. Reachability is limited to engine runs that happen milliseconds apart with changing data, e.g. the backlog consumed after a restart (XREADGROUP count 10) or several stream messages arriving together.
