title: Login lockout counter uses read-modify-write with an absolute value, so parallel failures do not accumulate
evidence: OpsUserService.java:34-35 reads failed_count; :46 `int failed = ((Number) r.get("failed_count")).intValue() + 1;` and :50 `UPDATE ops_user SET failed_count = :f WHERE id = :id` (absolute write, no row lock). BCrypt(12) verification (~250 ms) sits between the read and the write.
failure_scenario: 10 concurrent wrong-password requests (within the 10/min/IP limiter, or spread over several IPs) all read failed_count=0 and all write 1, so the account never reaches MAX_FAILED=5 and is never locked. The lockout guarantee holds only for strictly sequential attempts.
fix: Use an atomic update: `UPDATE ops_user SET failed_count = failed_count + 1, locked_until = CASE WHEN failed_count + 1 >= 5 THEN now() + interval '15 min' ELSE locked_until END WHERE id = :id RETURNING failed_count`, or SELECT ... FOR UPDATE inside a transaction.
reason: Confirmed. OpsUserService.java:34-35 reads failed_count, and BCrypt verification (:45) sits between that read and the absolute write at :50 `SET failed_count = :f`, with no row lock. Parallel failures within the 10/min/IP login limit (OpsSessionController.java:53) all write the same value, so the count grows by about 1 per burst instead of per attempt, and MAX_FAILED is reached far later. Exposure is local only (edge bound to 127.0.0.1:8700), so the severity is low.
fix_v: Replace the read-modify-write with an atomic statement: `UPDATE ops_user SET failed_count = CASE WHEN failed_count + 1 >= :max THEN 0 ELSE failed_count + 1 END, locked_until = CASE WHEN failed_count + 1 >= :max THEN now() + make_interval(mins => :m) ELSE locked_until END WHERE id = :id`.

title: Aircraft 'touch' runs about 9,000 sequential autocommit upserts on the stream-consumer thread before WS fan-out, delaying every global update by about 2 s; a DB outage stalls the realtime path by 5 s per snapshot
evidence: TrackWriter.java:52-61 is a synchronous @EventListener on the StreamConsumer thread: `for (AircraftState s : e.current().states().values()) { if (!queue.offer(s)) {...} } aircraft.touch(e.current().states().values());`. AircraftRepository.java:23-37 filters `now - lastTouched... > 60_000`. Global snapshots arrive every ~123 s, so every hex is due each time. It then runs one statement per aircraft: `for (AircraftState s : due) { db.sql("INSERT INTO aircraft ... ON CONFLICT (hex) DO UPDATE ...")...update(); ...}`. Each statement is autocommit, and there is no batching or transaction. application.yml:14 sets `connection-timeout: 5000`. None of the listeners has @Order, and TrackWriter (persist) runs before WsHub (ws). Measured on the running stack: global stream entry 11:46:11.212, engine log 11:46:11.332, then the WS diff `srv_ts=11:46:13.305` (+2.0 s after the engine). A region entry at 11:46:16.824 gets its WS diff at 11:46:16.869 (45 ms). skywx_stream_process_seconds_max is 2.20–2.43 s, while engine max is 70–88 ms and ws_fanout max 4–42 ms. hikaricp_connections_usage_seconds_count rose 92,060 → 138,737 in ~13 min (+~8,900 per global snapshot). pg_stat_user_tables: aircraft n_tup_upd=488,174 for 18,722 live rows; pg_stat_database xact_commit=555,222.
failure_scenario: (1) Every OpenSky snapshot (9,000+ aircraft) reaches WS clients about 2.0–2.4 s after ingest, which misses NFR-01 (p95 ≤ 1.5 s). The delay grows with DB latency: at 0.5 ms per round trip it is ~4.5 s. (2) If Postgres is down or slow, each snapshot (region every ~11 s) blocks for Hikari's 5 s connection-timeout inside touch() before WsHub.onSnapshot runs. Every user's map then updates at least 5 s late. The inline comment says the opposite ('DB 장애는 실시간 경로를 막지 않는다'). The 5 s repeats on every snapshot because lastTouched is not updated when the call fails.
fix: Take DB work off the ingest thread. Enqueue the snapshot and let TrackWriter's own virtual thread do the upsert as ONE statement per batch inside one transaction, e.g. `INSERT INTO aircraft (...) SELECT * FROM unnest(:hex::text[], :reg::text[], ...) ON CONFLICT (hex) DO UPDATE SET last_seen=EXCLUDED.last_seen, ... WHERE aircraft.last_seen < EXCLUDED.last_seen - interval '10 minutes' OR aircraft.registration IS DISTINCT FROM COALESCE(EXCLUDED.registration, aircraft.registration) ...`. Raise the per-hex touch interval to 10–15 min. Annotate WsHub.onSnapshot and EngineService.onSnapshot with @Order(HIGHEST_PRECEDENCE) so fan-out never waits on persistence. Keep all persistence listeners non-blocking (queue offer only).
reason: Confirmed. TrackWriter.java:52-62 is a synchronous @EventListener on the stream-consumer thread and ends with `aircraft.touch(e.current().states().values())`. AircraftRepository.java:21-37 then runs one autocommit `db.sql("INSERT INTO aircraft ... ON CONFLICT (hex) DO UPDATE ...").update()` per hex whose lastTouched is more than 60 s old. Every global snapshot (~123 s apart) therefore upserts all ~9.3k hexes. StreamConsumer.process() times the whole listener chain (StreamConsumer.java:177-195). Live metrics: skywx_stream_process_seconds p95 2.42 s, max 2.53 s, while skywx_engine_cycle_seconds max is 0.077 s and skywx_ws_fanout_seconds max is 0.023 s. The engine log line lands ~127 ms after the global XADD (entry 1790510799355 = 12:06:39.355, engine log 12:06:39.482), so the engine listener runs first and the remaining ~2.3 s is TrackWriter.touch before WsHub. hikaricp usage count is 225,208. pg_stat_user_tables shows aircraft n_tup_upd 606,130 for 20,536 rows. DB-outage path: the catch at AircraftRepository.java:38 swallows the Hikari timeout only after connection-timeout 5000 ms (application.yml:14). lastTouched is not updated, so every region snapshot blocks ~5 s before fan-out. That contradicts design 5.1 ('DB 종료·느림 … 실시간 경로는 DB에 의존하지 않음') and the class comment. Rewrite AircraftRepository.touch as a single JdbcTemplate.batchUpdate over the due rows, and add reWriteBatchedInserts=true to hikari data-source-properties. Alternatively use one `INSERT ... SELECT * FROM unnest(...) ON CONFLICT ...` statement. Raise the per-hex interval to ≥10 min. Mark a hex as touched before attempting (or back off globally after a failure) so an outage does not retry every snapshot. title: WS version contiguity check drops valid diffs: the server skips sending (empty diff, or global snapshot for non-world sessions) but the client treats the v-gap as a desync, discards the diff and waits for a full resync
evidence: SnapshotStore.nextVersion() is one global counter shared by the region and global scopes. WsHub.java:157 `if (diff == null || diff.isEmpty()) { s.lastSentVersion = version; return; }` advances the version without sending anything. The committed HEAD also has `if (global && !s.world) continue;` in onSnapshot; the uncommitted working tree removes it. ws-protocol.ts: `return incomingV > lastV + 1 || incomingV <= lastV;`. ws.ts:92 `if (needsResync(this.lastV, v)) { this.resync(); return; }` never applies the diff. Measured on the running stack with a region session (bbox 118,31,137,41, zoom 6): `11:56:08.2 snapshot v=214` → `11:56:30.5 diff v=216 lastV=214 up=110 rm=10 GAP->resync` → `11:56:41.2 snapshot v=217`. v=215 was the global snapshot (stream entry 11:56:26.958) and was never sent to the region session.
failure_scenario: Running build: after every global snapshot (~every 123 s), every region client discards the next region diff and only catches up at the following full snapshot ~11 s later. So ~1 of every 11–12 region updates (8–9%) arrives ~11 s late, which structurally breaks NFR-01 (p95 ≤ 1.5 s) and adds an extra full snapshot per client per 2 min. Working tree: the global skip is gone, but line 157 remains. A client zoomed to an airport or a quiet area (e.g. zoom 10, parked or no aircraft, so empty diffs are common) discards the first non-empty diff after any quiet cycle and forces a resync.
fix: Make contiguity per session rather than per global counter. Add `base_v` to DiffMsg: the version this diff is relative to, i.e. the last version actually delivered to this session. The client applies the diff iff `base_v === lastV`, otherwise it resyncs. Do not advance `s.lastSentVersion` when nothing was sent (line 157), or send a tiny `{type:"tick",v}` when the diff is empty. Add a unit test covering an empty diff and a global/region interleave.
reason: Confirmed. The version is one global counter: SnapshotStore.java:19 `nextVersion()` is used for both region and global scopes. The client requires strictly contiguous v: ws-protocol.ts:10 `incomingV > lastV + 1 || incomingV <= lastV`. On a gap, ws.ts:92 discards the diff and sends 'resync'. The server handles resync only by setting a flag (SkyWsHandler.java:79 `s.needsResync = true`), so the full snapshot waits for the next ingest event (~10-11 s later). The committed and running build still skips global snapshots for non-world sessions (git diff shows removed `if (global && !s.world) continue;`), which forces a gap after every global snapshot. The auditor's trace (v214 → diff v216 GAP → snapshot v217 ~11 s later) matches this code path. In the working tree the skip is gone, but WsHub.java:157 `if (diff == null || diff.isEmpty()) { s.lastSentVersion = version; return; }` still advances nothing on the client. Any cycle with an empty diff therefore makes the next non-empty diff look like a gap. Examples: a zoomed-in airport view, or a small Korean bbox where every global aircraft is overridden by region states. s.lastSentVersion is never read anywhere, so the server has no per-session base version.
fix_v: Add `base_v` to WsMessages.DiffMsg, set from s.lastSentVersion (the last version actually delivered to this session). In WsHub.fanoutOne, change line 157 to `return` without touching lastSentVersion, and set lastSentVersion = version only after a successful send (line 161, as now). Client: in ws.ts, apply a diff iff `m.base_v === this.lastV`, otherwise resync. Update needsResync() and its unit test to the base_v rule. On the server, make 'resync' trigger an immediate hub.sendFull(s) on the pool instead of waiting for the next snapshot. Add a WsHub test covering an empty diff followed by a non-empty one, and region/global interleave.

title: Fan-out joins every session's send with an untimed f.get() on the ingest thread, so one slow or stalled WebSocket client blocks ingest, the engine and all other users (Tomcat blocking send, 20 s)
evidence: WsHub.java:108-116 (@EventListener on the StreamConsumer thread): `fs.add(pool.submit(() -> fanoutOne(s, ...))); ... for (var f : fs) { try { f.get(); } ... }` with no timeout. WsSession.java:55 checks `out.getBufferSize() > SEND_BUFFER_LIMIT / 2`, then line 65 calls `out.sendMessage(new TextMessage(json))`. Disassembly of spring-websocket 7.0.9 `ConcurrentWebSocketSessionDecorator.tryFlushMessageBuffer` shows `bufferSize.addAndGet(-len)` BEFORE `getDelegate().sendMessage(message)`. An in-flight blocking send therefore does not count toward the buffer check, and the flushing thread blocks inside Tomcat BasicRemote.sendText (default org.apache.tomcat.websocket.BLOCKING_SEND_TIMEOUT = 20 s). nginx.conf:68-69 `proxy_send_timeout 3600s; proxy_buffering off;`. Measured payloads: world snapshot 861,673 B raw / 204,788 B deflated, re-sent every ~30 s.
failure_scenario: A client stops reading, for example a backgrounded mobile tab that keeps the socket open, a malicious client that never reads, or a link slower than the ~8 KB/s average of the world view. Once nginx and kernel socket buffers fill, that session's fanoutOne blocks in sendText for up to 20 s. onSnapshot waits on it, so the StreamConsumer thread stops: no engine cycles, no alerts, and no diffs for the other 199 sessions. Redis stream entries pile up behind it. Repeating with new sessions (5 per IP allowed) keeps the service stalled.
fix: Never join fan-out on the ingest thread. Submit per-session work single-flight: an AtomicBoolean `busy` per session; if the previous fan-out is still running, skip this version and set needsResync. Or bound the join with `f.get(200, MILLISECONDS)` and move on. Set session.getUserProperties().put("org.apache.tomcat.websocket.BLOCKING_SEND_TIMEOUT", 5000L) in afterConnectionEstablished. Close sessions whose send exceeds SEND_TIME_LIMIT_MS, and catch SessionLimitExceededException in sendOrDrop (it is a RuntimeException and currently escapes the IOException|IllegalStateException catch). Lower the nginx /ws/ proxy_send_timeout to ~60 s.
reason: Mechanism confirmed. WsHub.onSnapshot (WsHub.java:108-118) runs on the stream-consumer thread and joins every per-session task with an untimed `f.get()` (line 116). WsSession.sendOrDrop (WsSession.java:53-71) calls ConcurrentWebSocketSessionDecorator.sendMessage. I disassembled spring-websocket 7.0.9 from the local Gradle cache: tryFlushMessageBuffer decrements bufferSize before calling getDelegate().sendMessage(). The thread holding flushLock therefore blocks inside Tomcat's blocking sendText (default BLOCKING_SEND_TIMEOUT 20 s), and the in-flight message is invisible to the `getBufferSize() > SEND_BUFFER_LIMIT/2` check. The 5 s sendTimeLimit is only checked by other threads (checkSessionLimits). Those threads throw SessionLimitExceededException, a RuntimeException that the `catch (IOException | IllegalStateException e)` does not catch. It escapes, is logged at debug, and afterwards shouldNotSend() makes every send a silent no-op that returns true. A client that stops reading therefore stalls ingest, the engine, alerts and all other sessions for up to 20 s. That violates design 5.1 (slow client → 256 KB / 5 s cap → 1008). Severity lowered to medium: edge binds only 127.0.0.1:8700, so realistic triggers are a frozen or debugger-paused local tab or a misbehaving test client, and each stuck session costs at most ~20 s before Tomcat's timeout closes it.
fix_v: Do not join fan-out on the ingest thread. Add `final AtomicBoolean inFlight` to WsSession. In onSnapshot: `if (!s.inFlight.compareAndSet(false,true)) { s.needsResync = true; continue; } pool.submit(() -> { try { fanoutOne(s, v); } finally { s.inFlight.set(false); } });` and remove the f.get() loop, timing inside the task instead. In SkyWsHandler.afterConnectionEstablished, set the Tomcat per-session timeout: `((StandardWebSocketSession) raw).getNativeSession(jakarta.websocket.Session.class).getUserProperties().put("org.apache.tomcat.websocket.BLOCKING_SEND_TIMEOUT", (long) WsSession.SEND_TIME_LIMIT_MS)`. title: Predictions dead-reckon from the stale position as if it were current, so the ETA is overstated by the position age (up to ~4 min for OpenSky) and does not count down between global snapshots
evidence: IntersectionEngine.java:60-64 `path[0] = new Coordinate(a.lon(), a.lat()); ... DeadReckoning.predict(a.lat(), a.lon(), a.trackDeg(), a.gsKt(), i * PREDICT_STEP_S)`, and line 77 `Instant entryTime = now.plusSeconds((long) tEntry);`. `now` is Instant.now() at the engine cycle (EngineService.java:67), not a.seenAt(). Measured position age at fetch (track_point.fetched_at − ts, last 10 min): OpenSky p50 6.9 s, p90 22.4 s, p99 113 s, max 155 s. On top of that, the snapshot itself ages 0–123 s across the ~11 cycles that reuse it. AlertStateMachine.java:90 emits PREDICTION_UPDATED only when `|Δeta| >= 30`, so the displayed 'ETA m:ss' (AlertPanel badge) stays constant while time passes.
failure_scenario: An OpenSky aircraft observed 100 s ago (seenAt), 4 min from a SIGMET boundary along its track, is shown at the next cycle as 'ETA 4:00'. The true remaining time is ~2:20, and it does not change for the next ~2 min of region cycles. Aircraft that have already crossed the boundary since seenAt are reported as 'will enter'. This is a systematic bias, not a labelled uncertainty.
fix: Anchor dead reckoning at seenAt. Compute tEntry along the path from the observed position, then report `eta = tEntry − (now − seenAt)` (skip the prediction if negative), limit the horizon to `600 − age`, and set entryTime = seenAt + tEntry. Cache the path and the tEntry per observation (hex, seenAt) so later cycles only subtract the elapsed time. This is also the incremental design that fixes PERF-4.
reason: Confirmed. IntersectionEngine.predictOne (IntersectionEngine.java:59-80) dead-reckons from `a.lat(), a.lon()` (the position at a.seenAt()) and reports `etaS = tEntry` with `entryTime = now.plusSeconds(tEntry)`, where `now` is the engine-cycle time. The age (now − seenAt) is never subtracted. DB probe (last 10 min, fetched_at − ts): OpenSky position age at fetch p50 4.8 s, p90 14.2 s, p99 107.7 s, max 190.5 s. The same OpenSky snapshot is then reused for ~120 s of region cycles, and identical positions give an identical tEntry, so the ETA neither counts down nor accounts for age. AlertStateMachine only re-emits when |Δeta| ≥ 30 (line 90), and AlertPanel/EvidenceCard show the static eta_s. The result is a systematic overestimate of up to ~2–4 min on a 10-min horizon for global aircraft. Aircraft that have already crossed the boundary since seenAt can also still be shown as 'will enter'. The prediction is labelled 추정, but the bias is a computational error, not labelled uncertainty.
fix_v: In predictOne, compute `double age = Math.max(0, Duration.between(a.seenAt(), now).toMillis() / 1000.0)`. Skip the aircraft when age ≥ 600. After computing tEntry from the observed position, use `double remaining = tEntry - age; if (remaining <= 0) continue;`. Report etaS = round(remaining), entryTime = a.seenAt().plusSeconds((long) tEntry), altAtEntry from tEntry, and add `"position_age_s"` to the evidence. Add a unit test where seenAt is 120 s old: ETA must be reduced by 120 s.

title: World-scale WS sessions re-encode and re-send identical 0.75–0.86 MB snapshots per session every 30 s although global data changes every ~2 min; untested at 200 connections

Per client that is ~8 KB/s compressed, 66 kbps, 84% of it redundant resends.

Before relaxing the resync, fix AircraftState.changedFrom line 25 (`!seenAt.equals(o.seenAt) && quality != o.quality` should bump seen_at at least every ~30 s); otherwise parked aircraft go stale client-side. (3) Re-run the k6 WS test with ≥50% world-bbox sessions.
reason: Confirmed from code. WsHub.fanoutOne (line 154) forces sendFull every wsResyncIntervalS (30 s), even when the source versions have not changed. sendFull (lines 173-189) iterates all merged states, builds a new LinkedHashMap per aircraft via WsMessages.encode and serializes a per-session String. Nothing is shared between sessions. In the working tree every zoom ≤ 5 session is 'world' (SkyWsHandler.java:95), so each 30 s resync is a ~750 KB encode+serialize per session. Live JVM metrics already show 12 'G1 Humongous Allocation' pauses, consistent with >512 KB strings. At NFR-03's 200 connections this is ~200 × tens of ms of CPU per wave, and onSnapshot joins all tasks, so region diffs wait behind it (a projection, not a measurement; PERF.md's 200-connection test used region bboxes only). If it is queued while another send on the session is in flight, OverflowStrategy.DROP silently discards it, sendMessage returns normally, and sendFull marks the resync done. title: Every subscribe (each map pan or zoom) re-sends viewport-independent SIGMET (~108 KB) and all-alerts (~190 KB) payloads, rebuilt and serialized per session; status re-queries Redis per session

title: Frontend world mode re-posts and re-tiles unchanged aircraft every second: no interpolation is possible (no seen_at/gs_kt), yet the worker ticks and MapView calls setData on the full set

title: KMA radar job re-downloads and re-renders 3 old frames every 5-min cycle and discards them immediately; the render blocks the asyncio loop and the KMA budget is not enforced
evidence: jobs/kma_radar.py:88-91 `have = {f["tm"] for f in await self._frames()}` (the 12 retained frames) and `candidates = [tm for tm in listing.data if tm <= now_tm and tm not in have][-MAX_PER_CYCLE:]`. The listing covers the whole KST day, so this picks the 3 frames just older than the retained window plus the new one, and line 158 `[-KEEP_FRAMES:]` drops them again. Collector logs: 11:37:42 fetched 1915, 1920 (+2025, 2030); 11:42:46 fetched 1920, 1925, 1930 (+2035); 11:47:51 fetched 1925, 1930, 1935 (+2040). The same old frames are fetched repeatedly. Redis holds 23 `skywx:radar_kr:frame:*` keys against 12 listed. `_store` (async) calls CPU-bound `render_mercator_png` inline: kma_grid.py:141-142 creates a new Transformer and transforms 1152×1324 ≈ 1.5M pixels per frame, and line 158 uses `optimize=True`. Each frame takes ~0.85–1.0 s in the logs. main.py:66-73 `limits` omits "kma_radar", so `budget:kma_radar:20260927` shows `limit '0'`, which means unlimited despite config `budget_kma_radar: int = 1000`.
failure_scenario: Each cycle makes 5 API calls instead of 2 (1,440/day instead of 576) and spends ~3.5 s of single-threaded event-loop CPU instead of ~0.9 s. During that time the region aircraft job cannot run: on 11:47:43.7 → 11:47:55.7 the gap was 12 s instead of ~11 s. Orphan PNGs (~90 KB base64 each, 3 h TTL) occupy Redis. Because the budget guard is unwired, a listing or parse bug could hammer the KMA API Hub without limit.
fix: Select only frames newer than the newest retained one: `latest = max(have, default='')`, then `[tm for tm in listing.data if latest < tm <= now_tm][-MAX_PER_CYCLE:]`. The pixel→grid mapping depends only on (nx, ny), so cache `row`/`col`/`inside` index arrays at module level (lru_cache keyed by nx, ny) to reduce each frame to a numpy gather. Run the render with `await asyncio.to_thread(render_mercator_png, ...)`. Drop `optimize=True` (use compress_level=6). Add `"kma_radar": settings.budget_kma_radar` to `limits` in main.py.
reason: Confirmed live. jobs/kma_radar.py:91 `[tm for tm in listing.data if tm <= now_tm and tm not in have][-MAX_PER_CYCLE:]`. The listing covers the whole KST day, so the candidates are the 3 frames just older than the retained 12 plus the new one. Line 158 `[-KEEP_FRAMES:]` then drops the old ones again. Collector logs: 12:03:32–36 fetched 1940, 1945, 1950, 2055; 12:08:41–44 fetched 1950, 1955, 2100, 2105, so 1950 was downloaded and rendered twice. Redis holds 28 `skywx:radar_kr:frame:*` keys against 12 listed. The budget is unwired: main.py:66-73 `limits` has no "kma_radar" key, so Budget.reserve passes limit 0, and RESERVE_LUA treats `limit > 0` as the only cap (budget.py:13). Redis `budget:kma_radar:20260927` shows limit 0, i.e. unlimited, despite config budget_kma_radar=1000. render_mercator_png (kma_grid.py:132-158: a new Transformer per call, a 1.5M-pixel transform, PNG optimize=True) runs inline in the async _store, blocking the event loop for roughly 0.3–1 s per frame. The 22 s region gap at 12:03:30→12:03:52 was actually an adsb.lol 429, not KMA, so the event-loop impact on region cadence is smaller than claimed, but the blocking is real.
fix_v: kma_radar.py:91: `latest = max(have, default=""); candidates = [tm for tm in listing.data if latest < tm <= now_tm][-MAX_PER_CYCLE:]`. main.py limits: add `"kma_radar": settings.budget_kma_radar`. In _store: `png, meta = await asyncio.to_thread(render_mercator_png, header, grid)`. In kma_grid.py, cache the index arrays (row, col, inside) per (nx, ny, width) with functools.lru_cache, and create the Transformer once at module level. Replace `optimize=True` with `compress_level=6`.

title: Every ENTERED/PREDICTED alert re-upserts the full SIGMET row (GeoJSON, geometry, TOAST), and all SIGMETs are re-upserted every 5 min even when unchanged
evidence: AlertRepository.java:47-50 `case ENTERED, PREDICTED -> { var s = sigmetStore.get(a.sigmetId()); if (s != null) sigmets.upsert(s); ...`. SigmetRepository.java:38-52 `upsert` serializes the geometry to GeoJSON, calls `ST_Multi(ST_SetSRID(ST_GeomFromGeoJSON(:geo)...))` and `ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE SET ... geom = EXCLUDED.geom, ... raw_text = EXCLUDED.raw_text` unconditionally. Lines 27-35 re-upsert every SIGMET on each SigmetsUpdated (5 min). pg_stat_user_tables: sigmet n_tup_upd = 15,246 for 253 live rows. The 5-min path accounts for only ~5k (≈125 × 12/h × 3.3 h); the rest come from the ~7,500 alert inserts.
failure_scenario: With global traffic, each global cycle emits 50–90 alert events, and each one rewrites a SIGMET row with its polygon and raw text. That is thousands of redundant row versions, WAL volume and autovacuum work per hour. It also doubles the round trips of the alert-persistence thread.
fix: Keep an in-memory map of persisted SIGMET id → (validTo, hash of raw_text/geometry). Upsert only when the SIGMET is new or changed, and use `ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE ... WHERE sigmet.raw_text IS DISTINCT FROM EXCLUDED.raw_text OR sigmet.valid_to IS DISTINCT FROM EXCLUDED.valid_to`. In AlertRepository, rely on the SIGMET having been persisted (for example, persist SigmetsUpdated synchronously before the engine runs on it) rather than re-upserting per alert.
reason: Confirmed. AlertRepository.persist (AlertRepository.java:47-50) calls `sigmets.upsert(s)` for every ENTERED/PREDICTED event. SigmetRepository.upsert (lines 38-53) re-serializes the geometry to GeoJSON and runs ST_GeomFromGeoJSON with an unconditional `DO UPDATE SET ... geom = EXCLUDED.geom, raw_text = EXCLUDED.raw_text ...`. onSigmets (lines 27-36) also re-upserts every SIGMET every 5 min. pg_stat_user_tables: sigmet n_tup_upd 16,931 for 271 live rows. That is write amplification (new tuple versions, TOAST and WAL for large polygons) and extra round trips on the alert-persist thread. It runs on background virtual threads, so there is no realtime impact; hence low.
fix_v: Add a change guard to the upsert: `... DO UPDATE SET ... WHERE sigmet.raw_text IS DISTINCT FROM EXCLUDED.raw_text OR sigmet.valid_to IS DISTINCT FROM EXCLUDED.valid_to OR sigmet.base_ft IS DISTINCT FROM EXCLUDED.base_ft OR sigmet.top_ft IS DISTINCT FROM EXCLUDED.top_ft OR sigmet.excluded_reason IS DISTINCT FROM EXCLUDED.excluded_reason`. In SigmetRepository, keep a `ConcurrentHashMap<String,Instant> persisted` (id → fetchedAt) and make upsert() a no-op when the same id/fetchedAt was already written. AlertRepository then pays only a map lookup per alert.

title: REST /aircraft (working tree now merges global) rebuilds up to ~4,300 GeoJSON features (~1.5 MB) per request; the ETag changes every ~11 s even for bboxes with no region traffic
evidence: AircraftController.java:53-58 (working tree): `String etag = "\"v" + s.version() + "-" + g.version() + "\""; ... for (AircraftState a : snapshots.mergedValues()) { if (!b.contains(...)) continue; features.add(feature(a, ...)); }`. It builds new LinkedHashMaps per feature on every request, and bbox area is limited to 2,500 sq° (line 52). Measured: the region response is 37,449 B for ~110 aircraft (≈340 B/feature). The current OpenSky snapshot has 4,287 aircraft in bbox -10,35,40,60 (1,250 sq°) and 4,371 in 1,680 sq°.
failure_scenario: A client polling a Europe bbox gets ~1.46 MB of JSON rebuilt from scratch per request. At the NFR-02 test rate (100 rps) that is ~146 MB/s of map building and serialization on 4 cores. The region version bumps the ETag every ~11 s, so If-None-Match revalidation misses even though the Europe content changes only every ~123 s. The p95 budget has only been verified for ~110 features.
fix: Cache serialized responses keyed by (source versions that intersect the bbox, bbox quantized to a tile grid, detail). Build the ETag from only the versions that intersect the bbox: the global version alone when the bbox does not touch the region extent. Alternatively pre-bucket global states into tiles per version and stream cached tile fragments. Add a k6 scenario with a 1,000–2,500 sq° non-Korea bbox.
reason: The code matches the description (AircraftController.java:53-61 in the working tree iterates mergedValues() and builds features per request, and the ETag concatenates region and global versions). But there is no concrete failure. The web UI never calls `/api/v1/aircraft?bbox` (grep: only /aircraft/{hex} and /track are used). The map uses WS. The public endpoint is capped by the per-IP rate limit (120/min) and by max-bbox 2500 sq°. The '100 rps on a Europe bbox' scenario is hypothetical and not part of NFR-02's test, which used the Korea region. The region-version-driven ETag churn only costs a 200 instead of a 304 every ~11 s, and max-age=5 already forces revalidation. This is a 'could be better' item, not a defect. (The region-only meta on this endpoint is covered by PERF-6.)
fix_v: None required. Optionally key the ETag on the global version alone when the bbox does not intersect the region circle, and add a non-Korea bbox scenario to perf/rest.js.

title: Aircraft search is a sequential scan of upper(hex)/upper(registration) over a table that grows with every globally seen hex
evidence: AircraftRepository.java:49-53 `WHERE upper(hex) LIKE :p OR upper(registration) LIKE :p ORDER BY last_seen DESC LIMIT :n`. V1__init.sql:3-7 defines only `hex char(6) PRIMARY KEY`, with no index on registration and no retention on `aircraft`. EXPLAIN ANALYZE ('HL8%'): `Seq Scan on aircraft ... Rows Removed by Filter: 18504 ... Execution Time: 10.068 ms`. The table gained 18,817 inserts in ~4.5 h of global ingest.
failure_scenario: As OpenSky adds tens of thousands of distinct hexes per day with no pruning, the per-keystroke search (public, 120/min/IP) grows linearly. It takes 10 ms at 18.7k rows and is projected at ~50 ms at 100k rows. Several concurrent searches then compete with TrackWriter for the 12-connection pool.
fix: Store hex lowercase and query `hex LIKE lower(:p) || '%'` using a `text_pattern_ops` (or `COLLATE "C"`) index. Add `CREATE INDEX aircraft_reg_prefix ON aircraft (upper(registration) text_pattern_ops)`. Run the two prefix predicates as a UNION ALL so each uses its index. Optionally prune aircraft rows not seen in 30 days.
reason: The query does seq-scan (AircraftRepository.java:49-53; V1__init.sql:3-7 has only the hex PK). My EXPLAIN ANALYZE shows 14.5 ms at 20,536 rows. But no concrete failure is reachable. The web UI never calls /aircraft/search (grep over components/lib/app finds no usage), so the 'per-keystroke search' scenario does not exist. The endpoint is rate-limited at 120/min/IP. Growth is bounded by the number of distinct ICAO addresses seen, and even the auditor's 100k-row projection (~50 ms) stays well within the ≤300 ms miss budget.
fix_v: None required. If search is later wired into the UI, add `CREATE INDEX aircraft_reg_prefix ON aircraft (upper(registration) text_pattern_ops)` and `(upper(hex) text_pattern_ops)` in a new migration, and split the OR into a UNION ALL.

title: Collector scheduler uses a fixed delay after each run, so the region cadence drifts to 10.7–11.7 s instead of 10 s (global to 123–130 s)
evidence: scheduler.py:32-41 `await run_once()` ... `delay = ... float(base)` ... `await asyncio.wait_for(stop.wait(), timeout=delay)`. The sleep starts after the HTTP round trip (0.4–1.25 s in logs), and jitter is added on top. Stream entry times on the running stack: 11:55:10.40 → 21.97 → 33.57 → 45.14 → 56.45 → 11:56:08.18 (11.3–11.7 s intervals); global entries at 11:37:51, 11:39:54, 11:41:57, 11:44:01, 11:46:11 (123–130 s).
failure_scenario: The design's 10 s region cadence (and the WS diff_interval_s=10 advertised in the welcome message) actually runs 7–17% slower. That adds ~1 s of average data age and makes each provider slowdown also slow the cadence.
fix: Schedule on a fixed-rate grid: `next = start + interval`, and sleep `max(0, next - loop.time())` plus small jitter. Skip a tick rather than bunching when a run overruns.
reason: The code does use a fixed delay after each run (scheduler.py:32-41), and region intervals are 10.7–11.7 s. But FR-01's acceptance criterion is '연속 60분 동안 수집 간격 p95 ≤ 12 s', which the measured cadence satisfies. The design's FR-02 constraint for global is the OpenSky credit budget (≤ 2,880/day), and a slightly longer global interval only lowers credit use. No requirement is violated and there is no concrete failure.
fix_v: None required. Optionally switch run_periodic to a fixed-rate schedule (`next += interval; sleep(max(0, next - loop.time()))`, skipping missed ticks) if a tighter 10 s cadence is desired.

title: The SIGMET layer is fully rebuilt and re-tiled on every alerts batch only to toggle the 'inside' highlight
evidence: MapView.tsx:137-147: the effect depends on `[sigmets, alerts]` and does `const fc = {...features: sigmets.features.filter(...).map((f) => ({ ...f, properties: { ...f.properties, inside: inside.has(f.properties.id) } }))}` and then `setData(fc)`. The sigmets source already has `promoteId: "id"` (maplayers.ts:32). An alerts_batch arrives on almost every engine cycle (logs: '1 events', '2 events' on most region cycles, 40–90 after global cycles).
failure_scenario: Every ~11 s, 125 SIGMET polygons (a ~107 KB collection, some continent-sized) are cloned on the main thread and re-indexed by the MapLibre worker, although only the 'inside' flag of a few features changed. This adds avoidable jank during map interaction.
fix: Call setData on the sigmets source only when `sigmets` changes. Drive the highlight with `map.setFeatureState({source:'sigmets', id}, {inside:true/false})` diffed against the previous inside set, and use `['boolean', ['feature-state','inside'], false]` in the fill/line paint expressions.
reason: The code matches: the MapView.tsx:137-147 effect depends on [sigmets, alerts] and calls setData on the full SIGMET collection whenever alerts change. But the load is ~125 polygons (~107 KB) about once per engine cycle (~10 s). geojson-vt tiling runs in the MapLibre worker, and the main-thread cost is a shallow spread and a postMessage. No jank or frame drop was shown, so this is a speculative optimization, not a defect with a concrete failure.
fix_v: None required. Optionally drive the 'inside' highlight via map.setFeatureState (the sigmets source already uses promoteId 'id', maplayers.ts:32) and call setData only when `sigmets` changes.
